    #167 The verdict in one module, saying only what it knows

    specced from #55real-use check #180real-green

    Specced from #55 (with #90, #95, the v1.2.1 gate's B1 and adjustments 1 and 2, #126's masthead, and the page's line limit folded in). The grill's seventeen rulings are on #55: https://github.com/OytunOnal/permit-rulebook/issues/55#issuecomment-6339075134. Bump Z (bug), no ADR.

    Specced from #55 (with #90, #95, the v1.2.1 gate's B1 and adjustments 1 and 2, #126's masthead, and the page's line limit folded in). The grill's seventeen rulings are on #55: https://github.com/OytunOnal/permit-rulebook/issues/55#issuecomment-6339075134. Bump Z (bug), no ADR.

    Repositories: both, the site and OytunOnal/permit-rulebook-data.

    Problem Statement

    A reader who finishes the interview reads a verdict that says more than the product knows, and points at things that are not there:

    • On the lowest salary band ("under €33,085.09") the headline reads "0 routes look open. One is short by €45,630/year." — the route's whole threshold given as the reader's shortfall. On the band above it prints the band's widest gap as a fact ("short by €4,274/year") while the rail beside it says "up to €4,273.64 short". One gap, two numbers.
    • The rail goes blank exactly when the reader is furthest from the line: "under €33,085.09" draws nothing, and "€59,373 or more" is a blue bar on one card and an empty track with a lone tick on the next, for the same answer.
    • "Steps that would unlock more" lists an intra-corporate transfer and a research hosting agreement beside full German recognition. A reader cannot take a transfer; their employer decides it. The hostile walk's headline names "a research hosting agreement" as the nearest step to a reader who declared a job offer in Spain.
    • An explorer with no offer reads "Nothing open yet — 8 steps would change that", none of which they can use, while 14 of their 23 not-yet rows say "Needs a job offer". The step is on the screen as a reason and missing as a step.
    • The step headings are set in the link blue and are not links; the three bordered counters read as tabs and do nothing when clicked.
    • The "criteria met" badge sits top right on a desktop and under a two-line title on a phone.
    • On a one-country path, Back from the verdict skips the last question: the verdict never writes a history entry.

    Behind them, the developer's problem: about 680 lines inside the page's bundled script decide which heading a route sits under, in what order, which sections open, and assemble each card from nineteen shallow *Html pieces. The two layouts compose their sections separately, a rule-shaped decision (isStepGated, "engine parity") sits in the site, a dozen reader-facing words are typed into the script, and the masthead's words share a file with the interview's flow. The page is 2,224 lines against a 1,000-line limit. Every fix above would touch the page, the card pieces and the masthead at once.

    Solution

    One module returns the whole verdict from the dataset, the answers and the arrival; the page paints it. Inside it, the verdict says only what it knows:

    • A bounded gap is "up to", in one exact form, everywhere it is printed. A band open at the bottom names the line ("needs €45,630/year or more"), never the threshold as a shortfall.
    • Every rail draws the reader's answer: a bar for a bounded band, a point at the rail's edge for an open one, with the card's own words beside it.
    • Steps are what the reader can do. A transfer or a hosting agreement is an arranged answer, said apart from the steps in one line.
    • An explorer with no offer reads, per country, what a job offer would do: how many more routes would be checked, and on what — never "would be met".
    • Step headings are ink; the counters are a plain summary line; the badge has one home at every width.
    • Every verdict writes its history entry, so Back lands where the reader was.

    User Stories

    1. As a reader on the lowest salary band, I want the headline to name the route's line ("One needs €45,630/year or more."), so that I am not told I am short by my whole salary.
    2. As a reader on a bounded band, I want the headline to say "One is short by up to €4,273.64/year.", so that it says what the card says and no more.
    3. As a reader comparing the headline with the card and the rail, I want one gap printed one way in all three, so that I can trust that they mean the same number.
    4. As a reader, I want a gap printed exactly, cents only when it has them, with its period, so that I can check it against the two quoted amounts it is the difference of.
    5. As a reader whose gap is €4,273.40, I want "up to €4,273.40", never "up to €4,273", so that "up to" never understates.
    6. As a reader on a band open at the bottom, I want the card to say "Asks €45,630/year or more on salary — your answer is under €33,085.09.", so that it names the line and my answer.
    7. As a reader on a band open at the bottom, I want the rail to put a point at its left edge captioned "below the amount", so that my answer is drawn where it lies.
    8. As a reader on a band open at the top ("€59,373 or more"), I want every rail to draw a point at its right edge captioned "above the amount", so that the same answer looks the same on every card.
    9. As a reader on a bounded band, I want every rail to draw my band as a bar, so that I see where it sits against the line.
    10. As a reader, I never want a tick on an empty track to stand for my answer, so that the rail never looks blank when I am furthest from the line.
    11. As an offer-holder, I want the steps block to list only what I can do (recognition, language, experience, funds), so that I am not offered my employer's decisions as steps.
    12. As a reader, I want "Nearest:" in the headline to name only a step I can take, so that the nearest step is never a transfer I cannot request.
    13. As a reader whose employer has a branch abroad, I want one line under the steps saying what a different situation would open ("With a different situation: an intra-corporate transfer would open 1 route in Germany …"), so that I still learn it.
    14. As a reader for whom no step opens anything but an arranged answer would, I want the headline to read "Nothing open on these answers." with its way forward, so that it does not count what I cannot do as a step.
    15. As a reader on the several-country layout, I want the arranged-answer line in each country's section naming only that country's routes, so that it sits where the steps do.
    16. As a reader, I want a country's tally to count only steps, so that "2 unlocking steps" means two things I can do.
    17. As an explorer with no offer, I want the steps block to open with "With a job offer in Germany: 4 more routes would be checked — on the salary it pays, and your recognition.", so that the one step that matters most to me is on the screen as a step.
    18. As an explorer, I want that line per country, naming what those routes would ask next, so that I know what an offer would lead to.
    19. As an explorer, I never want that line to say "would be met" or "within reach", so that nothing resting on questions I have not answered is promised.
    20. As an explorer, I want the headline's step count and "Nearest:" to leave the offer line out, so that the headline still counts only what provably changes a verdict.
    21. As an offer-holder, I never want to see the offer line, so that I am not told to get what I have.
    22. As a reader, I want step headings set in ink, so that I do not click them expecting a link.
    23. As a reader, I want the counters ("1 open · 0 within reach · 7 not yet") as a plain line with no border, so that they do not read as tabs.
    24. As a reader on a phone or a desktop, I want the status badge on the card's first line, above the title, beside the country's name, so that it is in one place at every width and read first.
    25. As a reader on the one-country layout, I want the badge alone on that first line, so that the card still opens with its status.
    26. As a reader on a phone, I want the first paint to hold still when the badge moves, so that nothing jumps under my thumb.
    27. As a reader on a one-country path, I want Back from the verdict to land on the last question I answered, so that I can change it.
    28. As a reader on any path, I want every verdict to be one entry in the browser's history, so that Back and Forward behave the same on both layouts.
    29. As a reader who came from a route page, I want that route marked and first in its group, as today, so that the move changes nothing I rely on.
    30. As a reader, I want every verdict word I read to be the product's copy, so that a word is changed in one place and said the same everywhere.
    31. As a reader of a not-yet group, I want "N routes need a job offer — see the steps above" to point up only when something stands above, so that it never points at nothing.
    32. As a screen-reader user, I want the verdict announced as today, from the same masthead it draws, so that what I hear is what is written.
    33. As a keyboard user, I want the headline to take the focus after a verdict as today, so that I do not tab through the header to reach it.
    34. As the developer, I want one call that returns the whole verdict as data, so that grouping, order and open state are tested in Node.
    35. As the developer, I want one call that turns the verdict into the body the page paints, so that the markup is tested without a browser.
    36. As the developer, I want the card pieces internal to the verdict module, so that a card block changes in one place and tests reach it only through the entry.
    37. As the developer, I want the verdict screen's masthead inside the verdict module, so that the headline and "Nearest:" are composed beside the sections they summarise.
    38. As the developer, I want the question screens' masthead beside the question card, so that the verdict module carries no interview words.
    39. As the developer, I want the interview's flow and history file to hold no words, so that it is one level and its exception goes.
    40. As the developer, I want whether a path answer is a step to be a property of the dataset, so that no list of fields lives in the site.
    41. As the developer, I want the offer line's count computed by the engine beside unlocks, so that both counterfactuals live in the domain and are tested there.
    42. As the developer, I want the step-gated decision computed by the engine, so that no rule is decided in the site.
    43. As the developer, I want the verdict's styles beside the module, from tokens.css, so that the card's look and its markup change together.
    44. As the developer, I want the page smaller by the verdict's code and styles, and what is still over 1,000 lines written onto #56, so that the limit has an owner.
    45. As the developer, I want the move proven to change nothing before any fix lands, so that a review can tell a deliberate change from a slip.
    46. As the maintainer of the dataset, I want a transfer and a hosting agreement marked as arranged answers in the dataset, so that the screen's split follows the data.
    47. As the maintainer of the dataset, I want the new mark to be an optional field with a schema bump, so that the contract says it.

    Implementation Decisions

    The verdict module (rulings 1, 5, 6).

    • A deep module of its own folder, declared under Modules in dependency-rules.md, level presentation. Its entry exports verdictOf, verdictHtml and their types, nothing else.
    • verdictOf(dataset, answers, interview) returns the verdict as data. interview carries the id of the route the reader came from (nothing else of the arrival) and the interview's answered count. The verdict holds:
    • which screen it is: answered outright by a notice, or compared — as the flow's action (answered-outright or compare);
    • that screen's whole masthead: the headline markup, the subline, the subline with its door where it has one, and the sentence the live region announces;
    • the layout: one country flat, or country sections. A section has its open state, its tally and its groups (open, unsettled, within reach, steps, not yet, not open to your passport); a group lists its routes in order, each with its card's markup.
    • verdictHtml(verdict) composes the body the page paints.
    • Inside: the card pieces and the step arrangement, whole; the verdict screens' masthead (the result and notice cases, EXPLORE_SENTENCE, the headline's markup, the answers-checked line); the verdict-only parts of the situations module (unscoredTally, unscoredVerdict, leadCountry, leads, namedFirst); and the composition now in renderResults, the two layouts sharing one section policy.
    • Outside, imported inward: the quote, reason and gloss modules (shared with the other pages) and what is left of the situations module (the question card's).
    • The page keeps what has a side effect: painting, the arrival line (shared by every screen, #56's), the announcement, the landing and the focus, recording the screen, the listeners. renderResults becomes a call to verdictOf, the flow's advance, a paint, and the page's side effects.
    • Every verdict word moves to the site's copy module. No reader-facing word of the verdict is typed in the page or the module.
    • The card's boolean arguments (with or without the country, unsettled or not) become an option named for what it sets.

    The masthead split (rulings 6, #126).

    • The results and notice screens carry their masthead as data, from verdictOf. Only compare and answered-outright can produce one, so no question screen can carry a claim about a comparison — B4's guarantee, by type.
    • The question screens' masthead (the intro headline and both sublines) goes beside the question card; its words to the copy module. The page draws one or the other by the screen's kind.
    • claimsAComparison moves into the flow's test, its only user.
    • The flow and history file keeps the flow and the history, takes UnscoredVerdict, and is tagged application. Its exception in dependency-rules.md (v1.2.2) is deleted.

    Every verdict records its screen (ruling 4). The page's one paint path records the verdict's screen for both layouts. Today the one-country branch returns before it does.

    The gap (rulings 2, 3, 11).

    • One function formats a gap: the dataset's formatEURPer on the unrounded gap — exact, cents only when present, always with its period. The headline, the card's "Short by up to …", the rail's caption and a step's "would come within reach (…)" all print it. No rounding anywhere a gap is printed.
    • Whether a band is open at the bottom is read from the band (no lower edge), never from a list of fields.
    • Headline emphasis: a bounded band, "One is short by up to <gap>."; a band open at the bottom, "One needs <threshold> or more."; points, unchanged ("One is N points away.").
    • Card, on a band open at the bottom: "Asks <threshold> or more on <field> — your answer is <band label>." in place of "Short by up to …". Rail row: "below the amount".

    The rail (adjustment 1, ruling 11). Every rail draws the reader's band: a bounded band as its bar; an open band as a point at the rail's edge (left for open at the bottom, right for open at the top) with the row's caption ("below the amount" / "above the amount"). A tick on an empty track never stands for an answer. The cause today: a band open at one end is given an invented far edge (80% of the lowest amount, 130% of the highest), and where the band's real edge lies past it the bar has negative width.

    Steps and arranged answers (rulings 7, 14, 16; #90).

    • Data: the situation field's transfer and hosting-agreement options carry is_arranged: true, an optional option field named like is_fallback, is_unknown, is_qualifier. Schema 0.8.3. A job offer and the fallback carry none.
    • The steps block and "Nearest:" take only steps: improvable answers and path answers that are not arranged. The headline's "N steps would change that" counts steps only.
    • What an arranged answer would open is said in one line after the steps, in its own paragraph style, not a step card: "With a different situation: <arranged answer> would open <n> route(s) in <country> …". Alone in that place, under no heading, when there are no steps; per country on the several-country layout, naming only that country's routes.
    • Where no step opens anything but an arranged answer would, the headline is "Nothing open on these answers." with its explore sentence.
    • A country's tally counts steps only.
    • The not-yet group's "— see the steps above" appears only when the steps block, the offer line or the arranged line stands above it.

    The offer line (rulings 8, 17; adjustment 2).

    • On the explorer path only (the situation answer is the fallback), the steps block opens with one line per country: "With a job offer in <country>: <n> more route(s) would be checked — on <what they would ask next>."
    • The engine computes it, beside unlocks: a pure function of the dataset and the answers returning, per country, the routes a job offer frees from their only hard fail and the fields they would then ask (the questions left unanswered). Its name says what it returns (routesAnOfferFrees). "A job offer" is read from the dataset — the situation answer that is neither arranged nor the fallback — never typed.
    • It never says "met" or "within reach", is not counted in the headline's step count, and "Nearest:" never names it. The verdict module words it from the copy module, naming the fields by their short labels.
    • Adjustment 2's "N routes would be met" is not kept: computed as the other steps are, N is 0 in every country on today's data (the explorer persona: DE 4, FR 3, ES 2, NL 2 freed, none met).

    No rule decided in the site. The step-gated decision (a not-yet route whose only genuine failures are path answers, with no live unknown and no moot criterion) moves to the engine beside isPlacedElsewhere, as isStepGated. The verdict module groups by it; it no longer derives it.

    What looks like a control (ruling 9, F4). Step headings are set in ink, the step's name in bold ink. The counters lose their bordered pills and become a plain summary line in the strip's text style. Both from tokens.css.

    The badge (ruling 10, #95). On the card's first line, above the title, beside the country's name, at every width; alone on that line in the one-country layout. Nothing wraps differently by width or title length.

    Styles (ruling 12). The verdict's styles (groups, strip, country sections, not-yet rows, steps, card blocks, card frame, rail, gap and points lines, card foot, scope line) leave the page's style block for a stylesheet inside the module, imported by its entry (the page reaches it only through the entry), every colour from tokens.css, a size from it where its scale has one.

    The page's line limit (ruling 12). This slice takes out the verdict code and its styles and stops there (estimated ~1,300 of 2,224 lines). The build measures the page after the move and writes onto #56 a Done-when line, "index.astro is at most 1,000 lines", with the measured count and what is left.

    Order (ruling 13). The move lands first and changes nothing a reader sees. Each fix lands after it, on the moved module, red first. The data repository's change (is_arranged, routesAnOfferFrees, isStepGated) ships before the site's tickets that read it, through data.lock.

    Testing Decisions

    • A test asserts a decision, not content: which group a route sits in and in what order, which section opens, whether a step is offered, whether a gap is said as "up to" or as a line, whether a rail draws a bar or a point at which edge, whether the headline names a step. Where a test needs words, they are the copy module's, read by name. It decides its pass on the shipped dataset or one it writes, never on the shipped watch state.
    • Seam 1, the verdict module's entry, in Node (site). verdictOf and verdictHtml carry every decision above: grouping, order and open state on both layouts; the masthead (B1's three forms, "Nearest:", the arranged-only headline); the gap's one form; the rail's bar or point and caption; steps against arranged answers; the offer line's presence, absence and wording; the badge's place in the card's markup; the not-yet group's pointer. Every test that imports a piec

    Tickets

    • #168 The step-gated decision is the engine's
    • #169 Arranged answers, and what a job offer frees
    • #170 One call returns the verdict
    • #171 The card pieces and steps go inside the verdict, and their tests cross its entry
    • #172 The masthead splits by screen
    • #173 The verdict's grouping cases run in Node, and the page's remainder goes to #56
    • #174 A gap is said one way and drawn on every rail
    • #175 Steps are what the reader can do
    • #176 Steps look like steps, and the badge has one home
    • #177 Every verdict is one history entry

  1. closed on
    23 Oct 2026

    #199 The carry has one entry and one level per file, a linter holds the shape limits, and structure.json merges without a conflict

    specced from #37real-use check #207real-green

    Spec of #37, from its grill of 2026-10-23 (rulings 1–16 on #37). Bump: internal, no ADR (ruling 16).

    Spec of #37, from its grill of 2026-10-23 (rulings 1–16 on #37). Bump: internal, no ADR (ruling 16).

    Problem Statement

    A maintainer of Permit Rulebook runs the structure check, and it is red on one line that no exception can cover: the carry's folder holds five files at its root, and a deep module has one entry. Four more exceptions on the carry fall due at v1.2.3:

    • three outward edges into its log wording;
    • its flow, which touches the build directory and the clock itself.

    CODING_STANDARDS.md names the shape limits, but "review reads them until a linter enforces them", and no linter exists. A 243-line function, nesting of 4 and a 1786-line test file all sat on master. In #110 three of the six hard Standards findings were these limits, and they drove the fix round's largest rewrite.

    docs/spine/structure.json is generated, yet in #167's build it conflicted in five merges. Each was settled by hand-regenerating the file, because no hand can resolve it correctly.

    Solution

    The carry.

    • It becomes a deep module with one entry, and every file in or around it says one level that matches the level's definition.
    • Its adapters live beside it, outside the module, and the command wires them.
    • The structure check shows no line for the carry.

    A linter.

    • ESLint holds the six shape limits, and its run is part of the green.
    • The file limit is lowered to 400 lines, and every line counts, comments and blank lines included.
    • What it flags today in the carry, plus every small hit, is fixed in this slice.
    • Every other length hit is an exception with its issue and its version. A test fails the green once the version comes.

    The merge rule.

    • A merge takes one side's structure.json without a conflict.
    • The structure command is rerun after any merge that changed it.

    User Stories

    1. As a maintainer, I want the structure check to show no root-files line for the carry, so that the check is green on structure for the first time since it was set up.
    2. As a maintainer, I want the carry's four v1.2.3 exceptions gone from dependency-rules.md, so that v1.2.3's release finds no debt due on the carry.
    3. As a maintainer, I want the carry's entry to be the flow and its ports, at application, so that reading the entry tells me what a carry does and what it needs from outside.
    4. As a maintainer, I want the live site, the build directory and the clock to be ports the entry names, so that the flow touches no disk, network or clock itself.
    5. As a maintainer, I want the build directory's adapter to be one small file of its own at infrastructure, so that every disk call the carry makes is in one place.
    6. As a maintainer, I want the clock handed over as Date.now by the command, so that no file exists only to wrap the clock.
    7. As a maintainer, I want the HTTP adapter outside the module at infrastructure, so that the command can wire it without reaching past the entry.
    8. As a maintainer, I want the command to stay main and be the one place the adapters are built and handed over, so that its level means what the definition says: wiring.
    9. As a maintainer, I want the log wording to be a domain file of its own outside the module, so that the module, the adapter and the command each read it inward, and the entry's interface stays about carrying.
    10. As a maintainer, I want the asset-name reading and the digest list in a private folder named generation, after the glossary's Generation, so that the folder's name says what its files describe.
    11. As a maintainer, I want the entry to re-export the three domain readers (readAssetNames, digestListOf, readAssetDigests) beside carryAssets, writeAssetDigests and ORIGIN_VAR, so that their own tests keep their seams and reach them only through the entry.
    12. As a maintainer, I want the carry's tests to pass an in-memory build directory and a fixed clock, as they already pass an in-memory live site, so that the flow's cases run without a disk and without time.
    13. As a maintainer, I want the build directory's adapter tested over a temporary folder, so that the real disk work is proven once, apart from the flow.
    14. As the deploy, I want the carry's outcome lines and its zero exit to be exactly what they are today, so that a deploy reads the same before and after the reshape.
    15. As a maintainer, I want the carry's files each at most 400 lines and their functions at most 40, so that the module this slice reshapes already meets the new limits.
    16. As a maintainer, I want npm run lint to run ESLint over src/, scripts/, tests/ and the .astro pages, so that one command answers whether the code keeps the shape limits.
    17. As a maintainer, I want a file over 400 lines to fail the lint, every line counted, so that length is not hidden in comments.
    18. As a maintainer, I want a function over 40 lines to fail the lint, every line counted, so that long functions are found by a machine, not by review.
    19. As a test author, I want a describe callback exempt from the 40-line function limit, so that grouping cases is never split apart for a number. Each it body and each helper is still held to 40.
    20. As a maintainer, I want nesting deeper than 3 to fail the lint, so that bodyWithin-style depth cannot land again.
    21. As a maintainer, I want more than 3 parameters to fail the lint, so that a long parameter list becomes an object.
    22. As a maintainer, I want a nested ternary to fail the lint, so that a plain if is written instead.
    23. As a maintainer, I want an unused name to fail the lint in .ts, .mjs and .astro alike, so that dead names do not sit on master.
    24. As a maintainer, I want the .astro pages' scripts linted under the same rules, so that the site's largest file is not the one file the limits never see.
    25. As a maintainer, I want the lint in the green, locally and in the deploy workflow beside npm test, so that a red lint stops a merge and a deploy the way a red test does.
    26. As a maintainer, I want CODING_STANDARDS.md's Commands to name the lint and the 400-line limit, so that a builder finds the command where every other command is.
    27. As a maintainer, I want every small hit fixed in this slice (10 nesting, 15 parameters, 7 nested ternaries, 3 unused names), so that only length hits, each with an issue, are left waiting.
    28. As a maintainer, I want every other length hit written as an exception, one entry per file and issue, naming the rules it may break, its issue and its version, so that the green stays at 0 problems while the debt is named.
    29. As a maintainer, I want a test that fails once package.json's version reaches an exception's until, naming the file and the issue, so that a lint debt cannot outlive its date, as the structure check's debts cannot.
    30. As a maintainer, I want the exceptions placed where the work already is (#56, #142, #127, #184, #182) and the rest in #198, so that each exception names an issue that will remove it.
    31. As the v1.2.3 re-plan, I want #182's and #198's exceptions dated 1.2.4, so that the re-plan has to place both before that release.
    32. As a maintainer merging two branches that each regenerated structure.json, I want the merge to take one side without a conflict, so that I never resolve a generated file by hand.
    33. As a maintainer, I want the merge driver set once in each clone by one command CODING_STANDARDS.md names (worktrees share it), so that the .gitattributes line works with nothing run on install. (Amended at the fix round, 2026-10-23.)
    34. As a maintainer, I want CODING_STANDARDS.md to say: after any merge that changed structure.json, rerun the structure command and commit the result, so that the merged tree's stamp is the tree's own.
    35. As a maintainer whose PR shows GitHub's conflict on structure.json, I want the documented way out (merge master locally, rerun, push), so that the GitHub button's limit is not a surprise.

    Implementation Decisions

    The carry (rulings 2–6):

    ModuleLevelHolds
    The command, carry-assetsmainreads its flags and the origin variable, builds the adapters, hands them and Date.now to the entry, prints, exits 0
    The live site over HTTPinfrastructuretoday's liveAnswerOverHttp and bodyWithin, moved out of the module beside the command
    The build directory on disk, build-directory-on-disk (new)infrastructurethe build-directory port over dist/: list the built assets with their bytes, say whether one is already built, write a carried asset, write the digest list
    The log wordingdomaintoday's wording helpers, moved out of the module beside the command
    The carry's entry, carry.mjsapplicationthe flow and its three ports: the live site (liveAnswerFor, as today), the build directory, the clock (now())
    generation/, privatedomainthe asset-name reading and the digest list
    • The entry's interface: carryAssets, writeAssetDigests, ORIGIN_VAR, plus the re-exported readAssetNames, digestListOf and readAssetDigests.
    • `writeAssetDigests` writes through the build-directory port.
    • `## Modules` still declares the carry's folder.
    • The four carry exceptions in dependency-rules.md are removed, and the structure command is rerun.
    • Unchanged behaviour: the outcome lines, their wording, the three outcomes and the zero exit stay as they are. The deploy workflow's comment pointing at the carry's header is updated to where that text now lives.

    The lint (rulings 7–14):

    • The tool: ESLint with a flat config at the root (// @level main, like the other root configs), typescript-eslint's parser with no type-aware rules, and eslint-plugin-astro for the pages' scripts. Each is pinned to an exact version.
    • The rules, all errors:
    • max-lines 400 and max-lines-per-function 40, neither skipping blank lines nor comments;
    • max-depth 3;
    • max-params 3;
    • no-nested-ternary;
    • the unused-names rule (@typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars for TypeScript, no-unused-vars otherwise).
    • The `describe` exemption: the config carries one small local rule. It runs the core max-lines-per-function and drops a report whose function is the argument of a describe call. Files under the tests pattern use it in place of the core rule.
    • `npm run lint`:
    • it lints src/, scripts/, tests/ and src/pages/**/*.astro, skipping what ## Ignore skips;
    • it joins the green in CODING_STANDARDS.md (Commands);
    • it runs as a step of the deploy workflow beside npm test;
    • the Commands' "Lint: none configured" line is replaced, with the file limit at 400.
    • The exception list: it lives in the config as one list, one entry per file and issue: { file, rules, issue, until } (a file with hits for two issues has two entries, each listing only the rules its issue removes; amended at #200's merge, 2026-10-23). Each entry turns those rules off for that file only. The list is also exported so the test can read it.
    • Where the exceptions point (ruling 14):
    IssueUntilFiles
    #561.2.3index.astro, question.ts, history.test.ts, s37.test.ts
    #1421.2.3route-page.ts; the files of countryPage, dataPage, datasetLd, feedbackPage, notFoundPage, siteHeader, siteFooter; route-page.test.ts, identity.test.ts
    #1271.2.3dev-server.mjs, render-assets.mjs
    #1841.2.4card-blocks.ts
    #1821.2.4browser.mjs
    #1981.2.4s13, first-paint, s27, s30, s23, s26, s25, orientation, s19, record test files, and every other test file with an it or helper over 40 lines

    An entry lists only the length rules its file breaks.

    • Fixed in this slice (ruling 12):
    • the carry's files and its two test files (carry-takes-attested-bytes-from-our-origin, live-site-over-http) under 400 lines, with their functions under 40;
    • every hit of max-depth, max-params, no-nested-ternary and the unused-names rule across the repository, including whatever the .astro script adds once it is linted.
    • No new comment rule: CODING_STANDARDS.md's comment line stays as it is (ruling 9). Spine brings its comment rules.

    The merge rule (ruling 15):

    • .gitattributes gains merge=ours for docs/spine/structure.json, beside its existing line-ending line.
    • The driver is set once per clone with git config merge.ours.driver true, the one command CODING_STANDARDS.md's Structure line names; worktrees share it, and CI never merges. No prepare script and no script of our own: at the fix round the human ruled (b) on PR #205's Security finding, so nothing runs on install and nothing writes under .git but the person who types the command (amended 2026-10-23; the earlier prepare design shipped in #202 and is removed).
    • CODING_STANDARDS.md's Structure line gains two things:
    • the rerun after any merge that changed the file;
    • the way out of GitHub's conflict: merge master into the branch locally, rerun, push. GitHub's merge ignores local drivers.

    Testing Decisions

    • A good test asserts what a seam does, not how; expected values come from the spec or a known literal, never recomputed the way the code does.
    • Seam 1: the carry's entry, `carryAssets` (existing).
    • The carry's suites pass an in-memory live site (today's helper), an in-memory build directory (a new helper beside it) and a fixed clock.
    • Every case they hold today keeps its id and its outcome.
    • The domain readers' cases (asset-names, digest-list, and readAssetNames in pipeline) import through the entry.
    • The pipeline test's reading of the deploy workflow stays as it is.
    • Prior art: tests/carry-assets/.
    • Seam 2: the adapters.
    • The HTTP adapter's suite keeps its cases over a local server and imports the adapter where it now lives.
    • The build directory's adapter gets a few cases over a temporary folder: list, already built, write an asset, write the digest list.
    • Seam 3: the lint config, through ESLint's own API (new).
    • For each rule, one source text that breaks it and one that keeps it, linted under the repository's config.
    • The cases include the describe exemption (a long describe passes, a long it inside it fails) and one .astro script.
    • In the same suite, the exception list is checked against package.json's version: it fails once the version reaches an entry's until, naming the file and the issue. Its red path is proven with a version past an entry.
    • A case also checks that each entry still names a file the lint would otherwise flag, so a fixed file's entry cannot linger.
    • The merge rule is not a test. It is proven once and shown in the PR: two branches that each regenerated structure.json merge without a conflict, and the rerun stamps the merged tree (ruling 15).
    • Moves keep case ids: a file split or moved keeps its case ids and outcomes, compared before and after.
    • The structure check shows no line for the carry, and no root-files line, on the PR's tree.

    Out of Scope

    • structure.mjs --root (Spine #373) and Spine's own structure.json merge rule (Spine #280).
    • The length hits placed in #56, #142, #127, #184, #182 and #198: here they are only written as exceptions.
    • A rule on comments (ruling 9).
    • Type-aware lint rules, a formatter, and the data repository's lint.

    Further Notes

    • Real use:
    • the first deploy after the merge prints the carry's outcome lines as before, and publishes the digest list;
    • npm run lint is green on master;
    • the structure check shows no line for the carry.
    • Grill record: rulings 1–16 are comments on #37, written as each was made.

    Structure

    • module scripts/carry-assets @application — the carry: the flow and its ports (the live site, the build directory, the clock); its entry turns from application and infrastructure to application
    • module scripts/live-site-over-http.mjs @infrastructure — the live site over HTTP, moved out of the carry
    • module scripts/build-directory-on-disk.mjs @infrastructure — the build directory over dist/
    • module scripts/log-wording.mjs @domain — the carry's log wording, moved out of the carry
    • module eslint.config.mjs @main — the lint's rules, its local describe rule and its exception list
    • edge scripts/carry-assets.mjs → scripts/carry-assets — dependency
    • edge scripts/carry-assets.mjs → scripts/live-site-over-http.mjs — dependency
    • edge scripts/carry-assets.mjs → scripts/build-directory-on-disk.mjs — dependency
    • edge scripts/carry-assets.mjs → scripts/log-wording.mjs — dependency
    • edge scripts/carry-assets → scripts/log-wording.mjs — dependency
    • edge scripts/live-site-over-http.mjs → scripts/log-wording.mjs — dependency
    • seam scripts/carry-assets — production: the live site over HTTP, the build directory on disk, Date.now; test: the live site in memory, the build directory in memory, a fixed clock

    #208 The interview page is wiring alone: the interview, its history and the country search are deep modules, the arrival is one call, and every Back says where it goes

    specced from #56real-use check #217real-green

    Spec of #56, from its grill of 2026-10-23 (rulings 1–12 on #56). Bump: Z, internal, with P7, P8/P9 and F11 as fixes. No ADR (ruling 1).

    Spec of #56, from its grill of 2026-10-23 (rulings 1–12 on #56). Bump: Z, internal, with P7, P8/P9 and F11 as fixes. No ADR (ruling 1).

    Problem Statement

    A maintainer of Permit Rulebook opens the interview page and finds the whole interview in it. index.astro is 1,387 lines:

    • a 1,030-line bundled script holds the screens' state in a dozen lets, the browser's history, the arrival, the country search's glue, the landing and the beat;
    • a 204-line style block follows it.

    Two exceptions fall due. The structure check carries two mixed-levels exceptions due at v1.2.4: the page (presentation infrastructure main) and scope.ts (application presentation). Four lint exceptions on #56 fail the green at v1.2.3:

    • the page over 400 lines, with functions over 40;
    • questionCardHtml at 79 lines;
    • history.test.ts at 566 lines and s37.test.ts at 639.

    The interview's real failures were found only in Chrome. Another tab grew or shrank the record; an outside entrance sent Back off the site; the arrival moved France three times. The decisions sit in the page's lets and ifs, where no Node test reaches them.

    A reader meets four small faults:

    • P7: on an edit screen, "← Back" and "Keep this answer" sit side by side, and nothing says which goes where.
    • P8/P9: Start over opens question one mid-page, with the hero and the stamp above the fold.
    • F11: from /germany/'s "Check yours" with a record on file, the verdict comes back with nothing saying it is from earlier.
    • F11: Start over there asks "Where are you looking to go?" while the address still says Germany.

    Solution

    For the maintainer:

    • The page becomes wiring alone, about 170 lines at one level, main. It builds the browser's history adapter, hands it and the record's store to the interview, and starts it.
    • The interview is a deep module. Every decision it makes comes from one pure step function, tested in Node.
    • The browser's history is a deep module of its own behind a port, so s37's two-tab corners run in Node with a fake browser history.
    • The country search is a deep module whose controller holds no DOM.
    • The arrival is one call.
    • Both mixed-levels exceptions and all four of #56's lint exceptions go.

    For the reader:

    • Every Back says where it goes, and so does Keep this answer.
    • Start over lands at the top of the page like a first visit.
    • A verdict brought back from a kept record says it is continuing from earlier.
    • Start over on a country's or a route's address starts over in that country.

    User Stories

    1. As a maintainer, I want index.astro at most 400 lines and tagged main alone, so that the page's one job is to build the adapters and start the interview.
    2. As a maintainer, I want the page never to call window.history or touch the screen list, so that the browser's history has one owner.
    3. As a maintainer, I want the page's style block in a stylesheet of the interview module, imported as the verdict's is, so that 204 lines of CSS do not count against the page.
    4. As a maintainer, I want the page's script to be a few lines that call startInterview, so that the bundled module is the interview module's entry, not the page.
    5. As a maintainer, I want the record's store handed to the interview by the page, inside today's guard for blocked site data, so that localStorage is reached in one place.
    6. As a maintainer, I want the interview to be a deep module declared in ## Modules, so that the structure check holds what is private to it.
    7. As a maintainer, I want its entry, startInterview(ports), at main, wiring its own parts, so that its level is what the definition says a deep module's wiring entry is.
    8. As a maintainer, I want every decision the interview makes to come from one pure step function, interviewAfter, at application, so that the decisions live in one place a test can reach.
    9. As a test author, I want interviewAfter re-exported by the entry with its types, so that the tests reach the decisions through the entry, as the verdict's tests reach verdictOf.
    10. As a maintainer, I want the interview's drawing parts (painting, landing, focus, the beat, the ledger's wiring) at presentation, only applying what the step function returned, so that no decision hides in the DOM code.
    11. As a maintainer, I want each gesture named (loaded, answered, edited a row, back, kept, restarted, the browser moved), so that the step function's input is the list of things a reader can do.
    12. As a maintainer, I want the step function's result to say the next state, the screen, the lines, the landing, the beat, the save and the history move, so that the page's former lets become one value.
    13. As a maintainer, I want the screen transitions of today's screenAfter folded into interviewAfter, so that the masthead's one-writer rule (B4) is decided where every other transition is.
    14. As a maintainer, I want the interview's history to be a deep module of its own, declared in ## Modules, so that its rule can be tested without a browser.
    15. As a maintainer, I want its entry at application to declare a BrowserHistory port (read the state, push, replace, go back, listen for moves), so that the browser is an adapter and a test can be another.
    16. As a maintainer, I want the browser's adapter for that port to be one small infrastructure file beside the page, so that every history call the site makes is in one file.
    17. As a maintainer, I want the nine history exports to leave screen.ts for the history module's private domain parts, so that the screen list and the held-step rule have one home.
    18. As a maintainer, I want the restoring flag, the entry the page opened onto, the first held step and the rebuild on load inside the history module, so that the page and the interview never see them.
    19. As a maintainer, I want the history to tell me, before a click, where the screen's Back will go, so that its label and its move cannot disagree.
    20. As a test author, I want another tab growing the record, shrinking it, or starting over, tested in Node through the history's entry, so that s37's two-tab corners no longer need Chrome.
    21. As a test author, I want an outside entrance, a re-entrance and an entry written by the build before s37 tested in Node, so that Back never leaves the site where it should stay, and never stays where it should leave.
    22. As a maintainer, I want the country search to be a deep module declared in ## Modules, so that one control lives in one folder instead of three files.
    23. As a maintainer, I want the search's controller (countrySearchOf) to hold no DOM, so that typing, the keys, Enter and a click run in Node.
    24. As a reader using the passport search, I want Enter to commit the highlighted row and nothing else, proven on the glue as well as the state, so that the wrong nationality is never recorded in silence again (B1).
    25. As a reader typing in an IME, I want its committing Enter left to the IME, so that composing a name does not answer the question.
    26. As a maintainer, I want the search's DOM mount to be a thin file of three listeners, so that what only Chrome can check is small.
    27. As a maintainer, I want listbox.ts, the rows' markup and the class hint private to the search, so that nothing else depends on the control's insides.
    28. As a maintainer, I want every sentence of the search in the copy module, so that the page and question.ts type none.
    29. As a maintainer, I want the arrival to be one call, arrivalOf, returning the record after the move, the route that sorts first and the facts of the arrival line, so that the page's seven arrival lets become one value.
    30. As a maintainer, I want scope.ts at application alone, with the line's words and markup in a presentation file of their own, so that its mixed-levels exception goes.
    31. As a test author, I want B2 and "France three times" tested through arrivalOf with the address given as a string, so that the arrival is tested in Node, not in Chrome alone.
    32. As a reader on an edit screen, I want "← Back" to name the question it goes to, so that I know it steps back one question.
    33. As a reader on an edit screen, I want "Keep this answer" to name the next question, or say it shows my result, so that I know where it goes.
    34. As a reader on any question screen, I want "← Back" to name the question it goes to, so that Back reads the same everywhere.
    35. As a reader who pressed Start over, I want the page at its top, header, hero and stamp in view, so that it feels like starting again, not like being dropped mid-page.
    36. As a keyboard reader who pressed Start over, I want the focus on the first control without a second scroll, so that I do not tab through the header to begin.
    37. As a reader who pressed Start over, I want no beat on the first question, so that nothing refuses my first click on a screen I did not reach by answering.
    38. As a returning reader whose kept record opens on the verdict, I want the line "Continuing where you left off — N answers kept." with Start over, so that I know this verdict is from my earlier answers.
    39. As a returning reader sent by a country page, I want one line on my first screen, not two, so that the arrival and the return are not said twice.
    40. As a reader who answers, edits or goes back, I want no resumed line on the screens that follow, so that the line marks only the return.
    41. As a reader on /?country=de who presses Start over, I want my answers cleared and Germany put back on the record, so that the screen matches the address I am on and the button I pressed.
    42. As a reader on /?route=… who presses Start over, I want that route to sort first in my next verdict again, so that Start over does not lose what I came for.
    43. As a reader on a shared computer, I want Start over to clear the stored record wherever the address points, so that the next person never sees my salary.
    44. As a reader on a plain /, I want Start over to behave exactly as today, so that nothing changes for a reader who came with no link.
    45. As a maintainer, I want questionCardHtml split into three parts of at most 40 lines each (the lines above the question, the options, the exits), so that the question card meets the lint without an exception.
    46. As a maintainer, I want screen.ts left with only the Screen and Masthead types the verdict and the question card share, so that no flow logic sits beside them.
    47. As a maintainer, I want history.test.ts and s37.test.ts each at most 400 lines, every it and helper at most 40, so that #56's lint exceptions on them go.
    48. As a maintainer, I want the page's typed words ("You declared", "Start over", the description, the title) in the copy module, so that the page obeys the copy rule.
    49. As a maintainer, I want the two dev-only hooks (?dev-profile=, ?dev-probe=) deleted, so that no dead code moves into the new module.
    50. As a maintainer, I want the structure check to show no line for index.astro or scope.ts, and dependency-rules.md to lose both exceptions, so that v1.2.4's due debt is cleared a milestone early.
    51. As a maintainer, I want every #56 entry gone from the lint's exception list, so that v1.2.3's release finds no lint debt of #56's.
    52. As a reader, I want every screen, answer, edit, Back, reload and arrival to behave as before, except for P7, P8/P9 and F11, so that a reshape of this size changes nothing else I see.

    Implementation Decisions

    The page (ruling 2):

    • index.astro is tagged main.
    • Its frontmatter draws the first paint by calling presentation functions, as today.
    • Its script:
    • builds the browser-history adapter and the record's store (localStorage inside today's try/catch);
    • calls startInterview with them.
    • Its words move to the copy module: the frame file or the interview file, by who reads them.
    • The two dev-only hooks are deleted (ruling 12).

    The interview module, `interview` (rulings 2, 10, 11): a new deep module, declared in ## Modules.

    PartLevelHolds
    The entrymainstartInterview(ports): wires the parts; re-exports interviewAfter and its types
    flow/, privateapplicationinterviewAfter(dataset, state, gesture), the interview's state, the gestures, and what was screenAfter
    The drawing parts, privatepresentationpainting (draw, paint, say), the landing, the focus, the beat, the ledger's wiring, the verdict's paint
    Its stylesheet—the page's former style block, imported by the page as the verdict's stylesheet is
    • The step function's input: the dataset, the state, and one gesture:
    • loaded (the kept record and the address's search);
    • answered (value, and the label the next screen says was recorded);
    • editedRow (field);
    • back (the field the history said to show in place);
    • kept;
    • restarted (the address's search);
    • browserMoved (field, or the verdict).
    • The step function's result:
    • the next state (answers, asked order, the field being edited, the arrival);
    • the screen (a question's field, or the verdict);
    • the lines (arrival, resumed, set aside, just recorded);
    • the landing (for example card under the header, page top, none);
    • whether the beat runs;
    • whether the record is saved;
    • the history move to hand the history module.
    • Wiring: the entry hands the history move to the history module and the save to the record's store. The drawing parts apply the rest.

    The history module, `interview-history` (ruling 3): a new deep module, declared in ## Modules.

    • Its entry is application and declares the BrowserHistory port: read the current entry's state, push, replace, go back, listen for moves.
    • `openInterviewHistory(browser, { asked, showing })` returns:
    • pushScreen(field) and replaceScreen(field) (renamed from movedForward and redrawnInPlace at the fix round, ruling 3): a screen was drawn by answering (a new entry) or by any other gesture (the entry it stands on). The field is null for the verdict.
    • startOver() (renamed from restarted(), ruling 3): the entries go with the record.
    • Back skips entries that show the question already on screen, and backTarget names the question before them; the port's back takes a step count (fix round, ruling 1).
    • backTarget(asked, editing): the field the screen's Back goes to.
    • back(asked, editing): either "browser" (it asked the browser to go back), or the field to show in place.
    • onMove(show): the browser moved; the field to draw, or the verdict.
    • Its private `domain` parts: the screen list, the held-step rule, and reading an entry's state. They are the nine exports that leave screen.ts.
    • Kept inside: the restoring flag, the entry the page opened onto, the first held step and the rebuild on load.
    • Amended against the standards' "no boolean argument that switches what a function does": ruling 3's drawn(field, advanced) is written as two functions.
    • The adapter: the browser's adapter is an infrastructure file beside the page over window.history.

    The country search, `country-search` (ruling 5): a new deep module, presentation, declared in ## Modules.

    • Its entry:
    • countrySearchHtml(question, declared): the box and the empty list, out of the question card.
    • countrySearchOf(options, { chosen, classed }, onCommit) → { typeQuery(value), pressKey({ key, isComposing }), clickRow(value) } (renamed at the fix round, ruling 3). typeQuery returns a view ({ listHtml, status, activeRowId, expanded }), pressKey takes the key event's two named fields (amended against the standards' boolean-argument rule; ruling 5 wrote key(key, isComposing)) and returns whether it handled the key and the view, and Enter and a click call onCommit(value, label). It holds no DOM.
    • mountCountrySearch(root, search): three listeners that apply a view.
    • Private: the listbox state machine, the rows' markup, the class hint.
    • Copy: the page's three search sentences and question.ts' two move to the interview's copy file.

    The arrival (rulings 4, 8):

    • scope.ts is tagged application.
    • `arrivalOf(dataset, search, record)` → { record, scopedRouteId, line }.
    • line is the arrival's facts (the route, the country, rescoped, kept, asks), or null when nothing moved.
    • replayRecord and scopedFirst stay exported. arrivalFrom, countryArrivalFrom, destinationFor, destinationForCountry and arrivalPlan become private.
    • `arrivalLineHtml(dataset, facts, glossary)`, a new presentation file, holds the arrival sentence, the question phrase and the line's markup. It glosses the route's name with the screen's glossary.

    What the reader sees:

    • P7 (ruling 6):
    • every question screen's Back reads "← Back to <short label>", where the target is backTarget;
    • Keep reads "Keep this answer — next: <short label>", or "Keep this answer — see your result" when nothing is left;
    • the words are three entries of the interview's copy file;
    • the short label is the dataset's, the ledger's own.
    • F11, first half (ruling 7):
    • a verdict that is the first screen of a return onto a kept record carries the resumed line, with the ledger's Start over moved in, where the arrival line sits;
    • it is never beside an arrival line, and never after a gesture;
    • the record's format is unchanged.
    • F11, second half (ruling 8): Start over clears the record and the history, then runs arrivalOf on an empty record with the address's search, the same path the load takes. On a plain / this is today's Start over. The device keeps nothing after Start over on any address: the arrival's destination lives on screen until the next answer saves the record (fix round, ruling 2, after the Security axis's L1).
    • P8/P9 (ruling 9):
    • Start over's landing is the page's top on every width: smooth, or instant under reduced motion;
    • the focus goes to the first control without a second scroll;
    • no beat runs.

    Around the module (ruling 11):

    • screen.ts keeps only the shared screen and masthead types.
    • question.ts stays outside. questionCardHtml is split into three parts of at most 40 lines: the lines above the question, the options, the exits.
    • record.ts, first-paint.ts and gloss.ts are unchanged.

    The structure and the lint:

    • ## Modules gains interview, interview-history and country-search.
    • The exceptions for scope.ts and index.astro are removed from dependency-rules.md, and the structure command is rerun.
    • #56's four entries leave the lint's exception list.

    Testing Decisions

    • A good test asserts what a seam decides, not how, and not the words. The expected values come from this spec, the rulings or a known literal, never recomputed the way the code computes them.
    • Seam 1: `interviewAfter`, through the interview's entry (new).
    • Every gesture's screen, lines, landing, beat, save and history move.
    • P7's targets: Back's field from the history, and Keep's field or the result.
    • The resumed line on a returned-to question and verdict, and its absence after a gesture and beside an arrival line.
    • Start over arriving again on ?country= and ?route=, and today's Start over on /.
    • Start over landing at the page top with no beat.
    • B4's property walk, moved from screen.test.ts.
    • Prior art: screen.test.ts, the verdict's verdictOf cases.
    • Seam 2: `openInterviewHistory`, with an in-memory `BrowserHistory` (new).
    • Push and replace, Back past and on the first held step, backTarget, Start over.
    • An outside entrance, a re-entrance, an entry written before s37.
    • Another tab growing the record, shrinking it, and starting over and answering again.
    • Prior art: history.test.ts, rewritten through the entry, and the corners of s37.test.ts.
    • **S

    • #210 The country search is one module, its controller tested in Node
    • #211 The interview's history is one module behind a port, and s37's two-tab corners run in Node
    • #212 The interview's decisions are one step function, interviewAfter
    • #213 The interview page is wiring alone, at one level and at most 400 lines

    Found: 2026-10-25, the green on the branch case-names (a rename of 12 case names) ran while #230's first implementer worked in its worktree at .claude/worktrees/agent-…, inside the main checkout. npm test ran 177 test files instead of about 88: every suite twice, the builder's half-done tree included. It took 799 s instead of about 530 s and failed four cases, among them the worktree's copy of s37 (net::ERR_NETWORK_CHANGED on the beacon under the doubled load). git status shows ?? .claude/: neither the worktrees nor .claude/settings.local.json are ignored.

    The promise: the green proves the tree a commit would make (briefing.md, Green: "the tested tree stamped"; the tested tree is what git add -A and a commit would make) and nothing else. One writer per tree: a builder's worktree is its own.

    The mechanism:

    • vitest.config.ts keeps Vitest's default include and names no exclude, so every *.test.ts under .claude/worktrees/ runs with the main checkout's suite.
    • eslint.config.mjs's ignores (and docs/spine/dependency-rules.md's ## Ignore, which they mirror) do not name .claude/, so eslint . reads the builders' trees too.
    • .gitignore does not name .claude/worktrees/ or .claude/settings.local.json, so the tested tree would carry a worktree as an embedded repository and the session's local settings.

    A green on the main checkout can therefore go red, or green, on another tree's code, and does so whenever a builder is at work, as through all of #230's build.

    Done when

    • npm test and npm run lint on the main checkout read no file under .claude/, with a worktree present.
    • git status on the main checkout lists nothing under .claude/ with a worktree present.
    • Vitest's default excludes still hold.
    • The fix is its own commit on the case-names PR, beside the renames' commit; that PR's green passes with #230's builders at work.

    #230 Every browser case waits on what it reads, never a fixed time, and passes at four times slower

    specced from #224real-use check #246real-green

    The site's browser cases read the page after a fixed sleep: open a page or make a gesture, wait 300 to 1,600 ms, then read the screen. On a quiet machine the page has drawn by then; under the whole suite's load or on the two-vCPU runner it sometimes has not, and a case fails while the site is fine. There are about 222 such waits: 134 navigations that sleep after loading, in 34 files, 61 calls to a per-file sleep helper, in 17 files, and about 27 sleeps written inline.

    Parent

    #224, grilled on 2026-10-25: rulings 1–8 are its comments.

    Problem Statement

    The site's browser cases read the page after a fixed sleep: open a page or make a gesture, wait 300 to 1,600 ms, then read the screen. On a quiet machine the page has drawn by then; under the whole suite's load or on the two-vCPU runner it sometimes has not, and a case fails while the site is fine. There are about 222 such waits: 134 navigations that sleep after loading, in 34 files, 61 calls to a per-file sleep helper, in 17 files, and about 27 sleeps written inline.

    The cost so far:

    • The data dispatch's deploy on 2026-10-24 (run 40082762975) failed on two browser cases, s37's Back walk and the first-paint shift, so that day's page was not published (#140).
    • #223's green went red on an orientation case reading the menu before the header drew, and the 9-minute suite ran again.
    • #215's merger had no green full run because of an s27 and an s37 flake (#208).

    This is the third time a fixed wait has turned a browser case red, and the candidate returns retro after retro (#97). The rule it breaks is SPINE_STANDARDS.md, Tests: "A test waits on an event, never on a sleep."

    One failure may not be the test's alone. The first-paint case measured a layout shift of 0.0504 on /?country=fr at 1280x800: #main moved 272 px, and "footer had no room at first paint". That may be a real race in the page on a slow device, which would break the first paint's promise (#66, #71).

    Solution

    Every browser case waits on what it reads and moves on the moment it is there; a long limit stays only as a backstop, so a broken page still fails, and fails saying what never came.

    • The browser harness gives every case the same waits:
    • opening a page returns once that page has drawn;
    • a second way in returns at once, for the cases that read a page before its script runs;
    • a page can be waited on until a condition holds;
    • a page can be waited on until it is at rest.
    • No test sleeps; the lint fails on a new sleep.
    • Chrome can be slowed on request. The slice's proof is the whole suite passing at four times slower, as it does on a quiet machine.
    • The first-paint shift is reproduced with that slowdown and judged. If the page itself jumps, the page is fixed in this slice.

    User Stories

    1. As the human, I want a deploy to fail only when the site is wrong, so that a day's page is never held back by a test that read too early.
    2. As the human, I want the green to pass on its first run when the code is right, so that a three-line change does not cost two full suite runs.
    3. As the human, I want a red browser case to say what it waited for and never saw, so that I can tell a broken page from a slow one.
    4. As a builder, I want one way to open a page that returns once the page has drawn, so that I never pick a number of milliseconds.
    5. As a builder, I want a way to open a page that returns at once, so that a case can read the page before its script runs: the covers, the stand-in lines.
    6. As a builder, I want one way to wait until a condition in the page holds, so that a case reading something unusual (a request sent, a record written) waits on exactly that.
    7. As a builder, I want one "at rest" condition (no animation or transition running, the scroll unchanged across two animation frames, no request in flight), so that a case after an on-page gesture reads a finished screen.
    8. As a builder, I want a case that asserts nothing moved to read once the page is at rest, so that whatever would have moved has moved before the read, and the case still catches it.
    9. As a builder, I want a gesture that loads a new document to wait until a new document has drawn its first screen, so that the case never reads the old document or a half-loaded one.
    10. As a builder, I want a read made while the document is being replaced to be asked again, and any other error to throw at once, so that a Back off the site does not fail a case by its timing and a broken condition is not hidden for 15 s.
    11. As a builder, I want the backstop to be one named limit with its reason beside it, so that no case carries a guessed number.
    12. As a builder, I want the backstop well under the case's own timeout, so that a broken page fails with the harness's message, not Vitest's bare "Test timed out".
    13. As a builder, I want the lint to fail on a sleep written in a test, so that a new fixed wait never reaches master.
    14. As a builder, I want the lint to fail on a navigation given a time, so that the old way of opening a page cannot come back.
    15. As a builder, I want a timer inside an expression sent to the page left alone by the lint, so that a gesture scheduled on the page's next task still works.
    16. As a builder, I want the lint's message to point at the harness's waits, so that whoever trips it knows what to write instead.
    17. As a builder, I want the per-file copies of the sleep helper gone, so that there is one place a wait is defined.
    18. As a builder, I want s37's draw wait moved into the harness, so that every walker waits for a new document the same way.
    19. As the human, I want Chrome slowed on request by an environment switch, so that a busy runner can be reproduced on this machine.
    20. As the human, I want the PR to show one full green at four times slower beside the plain green, so that "passes on a busy runner" is proven, not hoped.
    21. As the human, I want the green's length unchanged, so that every slice after this one does not pay for the throttled run.
    22. As a reader on a slow phone opening a country link, I want the page not to jump as it finishes drawing, so that I do not lose my place or tap the wrong thing.
    23. As the human, I want the first-paint shift judged as the test's race or the page's, so that a real flicker on slow devices is not mistaken for a flaky test.
    24. As the human, I want a page fix, if one is needed, to come with the first-paint case red at four times slower before it and green after, so that the fix is proven on the condition that showed it.
    25. As the human, I want the cases that hold the page's scripts back to keep checking the moment before the interview's script runs, so that the first paint's promise stays tested.
    26. As the human, I want every browser case to still pass on a quiet machine, so that removing the sleeps loses no coverage.
    27. As a builder, I want the held-script cases to wait on what they read mid-load, such as the cover on screen, so that they no longer depend on how long the script is held.
    28. As a builder, I want the harness's own waits tested, so that a wait that returns too early, the bug class itself, turns a case red.
    29. As a builder, I want the lint rule tested through ESLint with the project's config, so that the rule cannot go quiet when its file globs drift.

    Implementation Decisions

    The browser harness (the module every browser case already uses for serve and withBrowser) owns every wait (ruling 1):

    • `goto(url)` sends the navigation and returns once the new document has drawn.
    • Drawn means the document is no longer loading. On the interview page, it also means the build's stand-in lines are gone, since the interview takes them out in the task that draws its first screen. A page off the interview has nothing of ours to wait for once it has loaded. This is s37's draw check, generalised.
    • goto takes no time argument.
    • `navigate(url)` sends the navigation and returns at once (ruling 7). It is for the cases that read the page before its script runs: the held-script cases, and those that wait on their own condition straight after loading.
    • `waitUntil(condition, what)` reads an expression in the page until it holds and returns its value (ruling 1).
    • A read that Chrome refuses because the page's context was replaced (the document is being swapped) is asked again; any other error throws at once, naming the condition and carrying Chrome's message (ruling 10).
    • Past the backstop it throws, naming what, for example "the question never drew".
    • The backstop is one named limit, 15 s, read every 50 ms, with its reason written beside it (ruling 4): already proven on the runner as s37's draw wait, far above any draw on a busy machine, and well under the cases' own 120 s and 180 s. There is no per-call override.
    • `waitUntilAtRest()` waits until the page is at rest, one named condition (ruling 3). The page is at rest when:
    • no animation or transition is running;
    • the scroll position is unchanged across two animation frames;
    • no request is in flight.
    • `waitUntilNewDocumentDrawn()` is s37's "drawn after", moved into the harness: it waits until the tab stands on a document other than the one left, and that document has drawn (ruling 8).
    • The slowdown switch (ruling 5): withBrowser reads an environment variable, BROWSER_CPU_SLOWDOWN, and slows every tab it opens by that factor through Chrome's CPU throttling. Unset means no slowdown.
    • The harness's default settle constant and the settleMs parameter go. The server's script hold (delayJsMs) stays: it holds responses back and is not a wait.

    The browser cases (ruling 8):

    • Every fixed wait goes.
    • After a gesture that stays on the page (an answer, a Back on the page, Enter, a tap), the case reads after waitUntilAtRest(). A gesture does its work in the task that handles it; only animation and scrolling come after.
    • After a gesture that loads a document (a link, a Back off the site), the case waits until a new document has drawn.
    • A case writes its own waitUntil(<condition>, what) only where its next read depends on something else, such as a request it expects.
    • The per-file copies of the sleep helper, the shared walker's own, and s37's private draw loop go.

    The lint rule (ruling 2) is added to the project's ESLint config over the tests:

    • a sleep, a setTimeout that resolves a promise, is an error; a setTimeout doing other work, such as a fake server holding a response back, is not (ruling 11);
    • a goto call with a second argument is an error;
    • the message names waitUntil, waitUntilAtRest and navigate;
    • the backstop inside the harness's waitUntil is the one timer the browser cases keep, and the harness module sits outside the rule's files;
    • timers inside expression strings sent to the page are text, not calls, and are untouched.

    The first-paint shift (ruling 6): the first-paint case on /?country=fr at 1280x800 is run at four times slower and judged.

    • If the shift is the test's race, the new waits close it and the page is unchanged.
    • If it is the page's own race (the footer or the ledger drawn late, #main pushed), the page is fixed in this slice. The first-paint case is red at four times slower before the fix and green after.

    This work needs the slowdown switch, so it comes after the harness.

    Bump: Z, a fix (versions.md, Numbers); label bug.

    Order (for the tickets): this is a wide change, sequenced as expand–contract.

    1. The harness's new waits land beside the old parameter.
    2. The browser cases migrate in batches by file.
    3. The lint rule and the removal of the time parameter land last, since the rule fails until every file has moved.
    4. The first-paint ticket follows the harness's.

    Testing Decisions

    A good test here asserts what a reader or a builder would see:

    • that a case reads a finished screen;
    • that a broken page fails naming what never came;
    • that a sleep cannot be written.

    It never asserts how many milliseconds anything took. Three seams, agreed with the human on 2026-10-25:

    1. The browser cases themselves (an existing seam). The proof is the whole suite green twice: plain, and with BROWSER_CPU_SLOWDOWN=4. It catches any case still racing the page.
    2. The harness's page object (new, one test file; nothing tests the harness today):
    3. With the scripts held back, goto returns only once the stand-ins are gone, while navigate returns with the cover still on.
    4. waitUntil throws after the backstop with what in its message.
    5. waitUntilAtRest() waits through a running transition.

    This seam catches a wait that returns too early.

    1. The lint rule, through ESLint's own API with the project's config (new):
    2. a sleep in a test file is an error, while a fake server's held response is not;
    3. goto(url, 900) is an error;
    4. a setTimeout inside a string sent to the page is not.

    It catches the rule going quiet.

    The first-paint judgment uses seam 1's existing first-paint case, run at four times slower: red before any page fix, green after.

    Prior art:

    • s37's draw wait (whereOnceDrawnAfter, from #208's fix round) is the model for goto and for a new document drawn.
    • The footer case's layout read waits until two reads agree, the closest existing cousin of at rest.
    • The held-script cases (serve(dist, { delayJsMs })) are prior art for seam 2's held page.

    Out of Scope

    • smoke.test.ts's net::ERR_NETWORK_CHANGED in #223's red run: the machine's network changed mid-run; that is the environment, not a wait.
    • A slowed run as a green step, or on a schedule in CI (ruling 5): the lint rule keeps new sleeps out, and the green stays about 9 minutes.
    • The data repository's timing cases, such as s36's slow-body budget (#116, part 3): another repository, another slice.
    • The suite's split into fast and slow projects (#116, parts 1 and 2).

    Further Notes

    • #116 part 3 names the site's s37 case "a record grown by 2 after a live walk in another tab, then a reload". This slice's waits cover it; #116 keeps the data repository's half.
    • No GLOSSARY entry or ADR: the waits are test-harness terms, not product language, and every choice is a two-way door.
    • Rulings 1–8 on #224 carry each decision's rejected alternatives.
    • ## Structure below has two lines, ruled at #231's report (ruling 12) and #236's (ruling 18): the waits are a module of their own, since the harness (scripts/browser.mjs) stands at its 407-line Ceiling. The lint config (eslint.config.mjs, main) changes inside its level, and the tests reach the new module only through the harness.

    Structure

    • module scripts/tab-waits.mjs @infrastructure — a tab's waits on what its page does: the draw, at rest, a new document, a condition with its backstop
    • module scripts/html-in-pieces.mjs @infrastructure — the harness server's HTML sent in two pieces, split before a marker, for the first paint's mid-parse case (ruling 18)

    Tickets

    • #231 The harness waits on what the page does: a draw, a rest, a new document
    • #232 s30, s27 and s20 read after the page rests, never after a fixed time
    • #233 s31, s13 and identity wait on what they read, never a fixed time
    • #234 s21, s28, answers, s26, s25, start-over, set-aside, s19 and orientation wait on what they read
    • #235 The other browser files wait on what they read, never a fixed time
    • #236 The first paint judged at four times slower
    • #237 No sleep can come back: the lint refuses one, and the suite passes at four times slower
    • #242 At rest waits out a smooth scroll that has barely begun
    • #243 The first paint's phone rows see a shift in the page's first moments
