    #247 Each script names one level, read from what it does

    specced from #127real-use check #257real-green

    Every file under the site's scripts declares one level from docs/spine/dependency-rules.md, and seven of them break that today, each under an exception that expires at v1.2.5:

    Parent

    #127, grilled on 2026-10-25: rulings 1–6 are its comments.

    Problem Statement

    Every file under the site's scripts declares one level from docs/spine/dependency-rules.md, and seven of them break that today, each under an exception that expires at v1.2.5:

    • The dev server's probe proves the server it started is this project's by finding the product's name on the /data/ page. The name is a screen word, so a script reaches outward into the screens.
    • Six commands (smoke, data-pin, render-assets, shot, measure-taps, check-base) each declare two levels, infrastructure main, because each does everything in one file: it reads its arguments, does the work, and prints the result.

    Read part by part against the definitions (ruling 3: a level is what the definitions make it, never one chosen so a rule stops firing), each command holds up to three levels:

    PartLevel by definition
    reads the command line, prints the result, sets the exit codepresentation ("the UI, CLI or HTTP handlers")
    drives the browser or git, writes to diskinfrastructure
    builds the adapters (serve, withBrowser, startDev) and hands them onmain

    presentation and infrastructure share a ring and may not depend on each other, so a command's CLI part cannot call its job; only main may stand between them.

    Two of these files also carry a function over the lint's 40-line limit, held in eslint-suppressions.json: startDev in the dev server (64 lines) and main in render-assets (68).

    Solution

    Each script names one level, read from what it does, and the structure check shows no debt on the scripts.

    • The dev server proves it is ours by a fact of the build, /countries.json, beside the /@vite/client check it already makes, and imports nothing from the site's source.
    • Each of the six commands becomes three files, each one level, its name saying which:
    • the job keeps the plain name (smoke), infrastructure;
    • the CLI is cli-<name>, presentation: it reads the arguments and writes the lines, and does no work;
    • the entry is main-<name>, main: it reads with the CLI, runs the job, prints with the CLI.
    • npm run <script> stays the same for whoever runs it; package.json points at the entries.
    • The two long functions come within 40 lines, and their suppressions go.

    User Stories

    1. As a maintainer reading a script, I want its level tag to say what the file does, so that I can trust the tag without reading the body.
    2. As a maintainer, I want every script to name exactly one level, so that the structure check's "a file names one level" holds over scripts/ with no exception.
    3. As a maintainer, I want the dev server's probe to need nothing from the screens, so that a change of the product's name or of the data page's wording cannot break the harness.
    4. As a maintainer, I want the probe to still refuse a stranger process holding the port, so that the 2026-09-07 failure (the smoke walk reporting the site broken from a stranger's 404s) cannot return.
    5. As a maintainer, I want the probe to still refuse the built site served statically, so that a dev-only failure is not hidden by a healthy dist/.
    6. As a maintainer, I want the probe to refuse a server that shows our name on /data/ but does not serve our /countries.json, so that the name alone no longer proves anything.
    7. As a maintainer, I want the probe's refusal to name the path it asked and what it got, so that a failed start says why at once.
    8. As a maintainer, I want npm run smoke, npm run smoke:dev, npm run data:pin, npm run assets, npm run assets:check, npm run check:base and npm run measure:taps to work exactly as before, so that nobody's habits or the deploy workflow change.
    9. As a maintainer, I want node scripts/main-shot.mjs [out.png] to take the README's picture as shot did, so that the record of the product keeps being taken the same way.
    10. As a maintainer, I want each command's job to be a function that returns what it found, so that a test or another script can use it without running a command.
    11. As a maintainer, I want each command's CLI part to only read arguments and write lines, so that the wording of a command's output lives in one place and does no work.
    12. As a maintainer, I want each command's entry to only wire the CLI and the job, so that what a command does at the terminal is readable in a few lines.
    13. As a maintainer, I want the file's name to show its part (plain name, cli-, main-), so that I know a file's level from a directory listing.
    14. As a maintainer, I want cli- to keep the meaning cli-deploy-finding already gives it, so that the prefix means one thing everywhere.
    15. As a maintainer, I want the tests' imports of the jobs (the smoke walk and the probe, the lock reader) to stay as they are, so that the reshaping does not touch the tests.
    16. As a maintainer, I want the social card's words and layout to be read by the assets' entry, not its job, so that the job, at infrastructure, never reaches into presentation.
    17. As a maintainer, I want the assets' job to draw in Chrome, write public/ and run --check, so that all of its disk and browser work sits in one file.
    18. As a maintainer, I want the two screenshot calls in the assets' job to stay correct (the transparent icon ground, the card's exact size), so that a re-render leaves public/ unchanged.
    19. As a maintainer, I want startDev and the assets' former main within 40 lines, so that their suppressions leave eslint-suppressions.json and the count cannot grow back.
    20. As a maintainer, I want the seven exceptions gone from dependency-rules.md, so that the file lists only debt still owed.
    21. As a maintainer, I want each script's usage comment and the docs that name a command's file to name the new files, so that nobody runs a file that no longer does the work.
    22. As the deploy workflow, I want the steps that run assets:check, check:base and measure:taps to pass as before, so that a deploy is not held by the reshaping.
    23. As a reviewer, I want every existing case to pass the same before and after, so that the reshaping is proven not to change behaviour.
    24. As a reviewer, I want the new probe case to be red before the probe changes, so that it is proven to test the new check.
    25. As a reviewer, I want each command no case ran before to have a guard case, passing on master before the split and kept after, so that a command broken by the split, or later, goes red on its own.

    Implementation Decisions

    • The probe (ruling 1). The dev server's check that the server is ours asks /countries.json, under the served root, and accepts only JSON whose countries is an array; the /data/ page and the product's name leave the check. The /@vite/client check stays, after it. A refusal names the path and what it answered (its status, or "not this project's country list"). The dev server then imports nothing from the site's source, and stays infrastructure.
    • Three parts per command (rulings 3–4). smoke, data-pin, render-assets, shot, measure-taps and check-base each become:
    • the job, infrastructure: an exported function that does the work (browser, git, disk) and returns what it found; it prints nothing and does not exit. What it already exports stays exported from it (the smoke walk, its checks and surfaces; the data directory and the lock reader).
    • the CLI, presentation: exported functions that turn the arguments into the job's options and the job's result into lines and an exit code; no browser, disk or process work, no import of the job.
    • the entry, main: reads the arguments with the CLI, builds what the job needs and runs it, prints the CLI's lines and exits with its code. Only the entry runs anything at load.
    • Names (ruling 5). The job keeps the plain name; the CLI is cli-<name>; the entry is main-<name>. The package.json scripts point at the main-* files; the script names do not change.
    • The assets (ruling 2). The assets' entry reads the dataset, the product's words and the social card (all presentation or data), builds the card's facts and HTML, and hands them to the job. The job draws the icons and the card in Chrome, writes them and the sidecar to public/, and runs --check against the facts it is given. The two Chrome screenshot calls become one in the job. Nothing moves into the browser harness (at its 407-line Ceiling) or into the Chrome locator.
    • Where a job writes (ruling 8). The data pin, the assets' render and shot take where they write as an option, defaulting to today's place, so their guard cases write into a throwaway folder.
    • The long functions. startDev comes within 40 lines by moving its parts into named functions in the same file; the assets' former main is gone with the split. Both max-lines-per-function rows leave eslint-suppressions.json; the suppressions' other rows for these files stay unless their code leaves too.
    • Levels and rules. Every new file carries its one // @level tag. The seven exceptions in dependency-rules.md's ## Exceptions are removed. structure.json is regenerated with the structure command.
    • Untouched: the carried-assets command and its deep module (#37's), and the deploy finding's CLI.
    • Bump: internal, a patch.

    Testing Decisions

    • A good case checks what a command or the probe does from outside: what it accepts, what it refuses, what it prints and writes. None checks how a file is split; the structure check does that.
    • Seams, agreed with the human:
    • The probe (notOurDevServer), in the smoke suite. Its three cases stay; the stranger case's expected text follows the new path. One new case: a fake server that serves the product's name on /data/ and answers /@vite/client, but whose /countries.json is not this project's country list. It is accepted today and refused after: red before the probe changes.
    • The commands themselves, through npm run. The deploy already runs assets:check, check:base and measure:taps; the suite runs the smoke walk through its job.
    • The structure check, already in the green: it fails on a file whose tag breaks the rules.
    • Same cases (ruling 6): every existing case passes under the code before and after the change, run on both and compared.
    • Guard cases first (ruling 8, `SPINE_STANDARDS.md`, Tests: "Before code no case covers is changed, a guard case pins what it does today"): before the split, one case per command no case runs today, each passing on master and kept after: data:pin (the lock it writes names the data clone's HEAD and dataset version), the assets' render (the icons, the .ico, the card at 1200x630 and its sidecar are written), shot (a PNG of the frame's size is written) and the smoke command (--dev and --dist pick the surfaces; a broken page gives a non-zero exit). Each runs into a throwaway folder in the OS temp folder, removed after, never into public/, data.lock or docs/media/, so the job takes where it writes as an option, its default today's place. Ruling 6's hand run stays as the builder's last check before the PR.
    • No cases of their own for the CLI parts' wording: the guard cases run each command through its entry.
    • Separate changes (SPINE_STANDARDS.md, Code: "A refactor and a change of behaviour are separate changes"): the probe's new check is its own ticket, apart from the reshaping.
    • Prior art: the probe's cases in the smoke suite ("the harness refuses to walk a process it did not start"); the deploy finding's job and CLI, the split this follows.

    Out of Scope

    • Gathering each command's three files into a deep module, as the carried assets are; the human: "sonrasında deepening ile birleşirler zaten" (ruling 4).
    • Changing the level definitions; an ADR making a program's entry main was ruled out (ruling 4).
    • The carried-assets command (#37's exception) and the deploy finding's CLI.
    • Any change to what a command checks, prints or writes, beyond the probe.

    Further Notes

    • #127's body named src/lib/copy.ts, lines 28 and 30–35 and v1.3.1; the word now lives in src/lib/copy/frame.ts, the exceptions sit on lines 29–35 until v1.2.5, and countries.json answers an object, not an array (ruling 1).
    • #230 just changed measure-taps, shot and smoke to open a page with goto(url) and then wait for rest; their jobs keep that.
    • #226's step 3 is this slice's builders using red-before and same-cases.
    • #221 (no error dropped with a comment) shares one file, the dev server, whose two dropped errors this slice moves unchanged; it stays apart (ruling 7): its concern is what each error becomes, decided in its own grill over both repositories, and this slice only reshapes.

    Structure

    • module scripts/cli-smoke.mjs @presentation — the smoke command's arguments (--dev, --dist) as surfaces, its report as lines and an exit code
    • module scripts/main-smoke.mjs @main — npm run smoke: reads with the CLI, runs the walk, prints
    • module scripts/cli-data-pin.mjs @presentation — the pin's report line
    • module scripts/main-data-pin.mjs @main — npm run data:pin: pins the lock, prints
    • module scripts/cli-render-assets.mjs @presentation — --check as the mode, the render's or the check's report line
    • module scripts/main-render-assets.mjs @main — npm run assets: reads the dataset, the product's words and the social card, hands the card's facts and HTML to the job, prints
    • module scripts/cli-shot.mjs @presentation — the output path from the arguments, the written picture's line
    • module scripts/main-shot.mjs @main — takes the README's picture, prints
    • module scripts/cli-measure-taps.mjs @presentation — each screen's lines, the total and the exit code
    • module scripts/main-measure-taps.mjs @main — npm run measure:taps: runs the measure, which serves dist/ itself, and prints each screen's lines as it is measured
    • module scripts/print-report.mjs @presentation — a command's report to the terminal: its lines on stdout and stderr, and its exit code, for every entry
    • module scripts/cli-check-base.mjs @presentation — the problems' lines and the exit code
    • module scripts/main-check-base.mjs @main — npm run check:base: builds under a base, scans, prints
    • edge scripts/main-smoke.mjs → scripts/smoke.mjs — dependency
    • edge scripts/main-smoke.mjs → scripts/cli-smoke.mjs — dependency
    • edge scripts/main-data-pin.mjs → scripts/data-pin.mjs — dependency
    • edge scripts/main-data-pin.mjs → scripts/cli-data-pin.mjs — dependency
    • edge scripts/main-render-assets.mjs → scripts/render-assets.mjs — dependency
    • edge scripts/main-render-assets.mjs → scripts/cli-render-assets.mjs — dependency
    • edge scripts/main-shot.mjs → scripts/shot.mjs — dependency
    • edge scripts/main-shot.mjs → scripts/cli-shot.mjs — dependency
    • edge scripts/main-measure-taps.mjs → scripts/measure-taps.mjs — dependency
    • edge scripts/main-measure-taps.mjs → scripts/cli-measure-taps.mjs — dependency
    • edge scripts/main-check-base.mjs → scripts/check-base.mjs — dependency
    • edge scripts/main-check-base.mjs → scripts/cli-check-base.mjs — dependency

    The cause. Chrome hands a page its layout shifts as soon as the frame is laid out, but its first-input entry later (Event Timing reports after the frame is presented). A later read finds the entry, timed before the shift. Ruled out: a timestamp out of order (every entry, once there, is timed before the shift).

    real-use check #273real-green

    Found: PR #244's Security review, 2026-10-25, outside its diff. The test harness's serve() (scripts/browser.mjs:110) decodes the request's path and joins it onto the folder it serves (dist/) with no check that the result stays inside, so a request for /%2e%2e%2f… reads a file outside the folder.

    Reach: the server listens on 127.0.0.1 only, and only the browser cases and the scripts that drive Chrome (measure-taps, shot, smoke, render-assets) start it; no visitor of the site reaches it. A page served under test could read a file of the checkout or the machine through it.

    The rule: SPINE_STANDARDS.md, Security, and docs/spine/threats.md's rows on what a page can reach.

    Grilled 2026-10-27; the rulings are in the comments below (1–4, 6, 7; 6 replaces 5).

    • The fix, in `serve()`: a path it cannot decode answers 400. A decoded path that resolves outside the folder it serves answers 404.

    #275 Every browser case, deploy job and real-use check opens the site through one browser walk

    specced from #182real-use check #287real-green

    Whoever drives a browser over Permit Rulebook, whether a browser case, a deploy job, a live walk or a real-use check, starts by writing their own driver. #180's walker wrote "a trimmed copy" of the harness's withBrowser, #162's walk did the same, and in #208's review the Spec axis wrote two throwaway scripts of its own.     Problem Statement

    Whoever drives a browser over Permit Rulebook, whether a browser case, a deploy job, a live walk or a real-use check, starts by writing their own driver. #180's walker wrote "a trimmed copy" of the harness's withBrowser, #162's walk did the same, and in #208's review the Spec axis wrote two throwaway scripts of its own. Each copy re-solves the same things: a fresh profile, the two screens, real clicks and key presses, layout shifts not caused by input, and the page's errors. Each also gets something wrong in its own way. A phone walk once ran at desk width while saying 390 (#217's real use), and a dead interview once measured as "0 controls under the floor" because nothing read the page's errors (2026-09-07).

    Within the code, the harness has several interfaces open. Its files are imported one by one, 26 test files and 3 jobs each serve the site and open a browser in their own way, and the layout-shift reading that #269 fixed sits in the tests, where no script can reach it. browser.mjs holds 4 lint hits in eslint-suppressions.json.

    Solution

    There is one browser walk. It opens the built site or the live site at a screen in a fresh profile, gives the walker real clicks and key presses, and returns what it measured: the walker's own result, the layout shifts of the page it ends on (not counting those caused by input), and every error the page threw or logged. It fails loudly when the page threw, or when the page's width is not the width asked for.

    The walk sits inside the browser harness, which becomes one declared deep module with a single entry. Every browser case, every deploy job and every live or real-use walk goes through that entry. Nothing else can import the harness's inner files, so the structure check refuses the next copied driver.

    User Stories

    1. As a session running a real-use check, I want to call one walk on the live site, so that I don't write a browser driver of my own.
    2. As a session running a real-use check, I want the walk to open the live site's address, so that I check what shipped and not a local build.
    3. As a browser case, I want the walk to serve the built site for me, so that I don't start and stop a server myself.
    4. As a walker, I want each walk to start in a fresh profile, so that no storage from an earlier walk changes what I see.
    5. As a walker, I want to name the screen as desk (1280x900) or phone (390x844), so that every walk uses the same two screens as the browser cases.
    6. As a walker on the phone screen, I want the walk to fail when the page's innerWidth is not 390, naming both widths, so that a phone check never quietly runs at another width.
    7. As a walker, I want the width check to run after the first page draws, so that it reads the width the page actually laid out at.
    8. As a walker, I want real clicks and key presses, so that the page receives the platform's own input, the kind CLS treats as input.
    9. As a walker, I want to tap an element by its selector, scrolled into view first, so that I don't compute coordinates myself.
    10. As a walker, I want each click and Enter to return once the page has reported it, so that my next step never races the page (#269).
    11. As a walker, I want the walk to wait on what the page does (drawn, at rest, a new document, a condition), so that no walk sleeps a fixed time.
    12. As a walker, I want the walk to return the layout shifts of the page on screen when it ends, labelled with that page's address, so that I know which page they belong to.
    13. As a walker, I want shifts that come after the page's first input and that Chrome marks as input to be left out, so that the walk counts what CLS counts (#269's first-input rule).
    14. As a walker interested in an earlier page, I want to read that page's shifts during the walk with the same reading, so that a later navigation doesn't lose them.
    15. As a browser case about the header, I want to name a region whose shifts are marked, so that I can tell a shift above the box from one below it.
    16. As a live walker, I want to leave the region out, so that a walk needs no knowledge of the page's layout.
    17. As a walker, I want the walk to fail when the page threw or logged an error, listing each one, so that a broken page is never reported as fine.
    18. As a walker, I want every error of the walk, across its navigations and tabs, each with the address it came from, so that an error on the first page still shows after I move on.
    19. As a browser case that asserts its errors itself, I want to say that errors are expected, so that the walk returns them and the case keeps asserting them as it does today.
    20. As a browser case, I want a tab's own problems() to keep its meaning (since that tab's last navigation), so that the 69 existing reads stay true.
    21. As a walker on the built site, I want the traffic counter's two local-only messages left out, as they are today, so that a local walk doesn't fail on a request that is fine in production.
    22. As a browser case about one tab affecting another, I want to open a second tab in the same browser, so that the two tabs share the origin's storage.
    23. As a browser case, I want media emulation, typing, Back, Forward, screenshots and the request list as they are today, so that no case loses a gesture.
    24. As a browser case about scrollbars, I want to ask for the platform's scrollbars, so that s31's case still sees them.
    25. As a browser case about the wire, I want to ask the walk to watch the network, so that the record's promise is still checked on what the page sends.
    26. As a deploy job (smoke, shot, measure-taps), I want to open the site through the walk, so that the jobs and the cases take their browser from one place.
    27. As a deploy run on a busy runner, I want BROWSER_CPU_SLOWDOWN to keep slowing every tab, so that the runner's tests stay as they were.
    28. As the asset renderer, I want to find Chrome through the entry, so that it doesn't reach past the module.
    29. As a maintainer, I want the harness to be one declared deep module, so that the structure check refuses any import past its entry.
    30. As a maintainer, I want the test server and the exit register inside the module (#245, ruling 7), so that what a walk opens is closed by the module that opened it.
    31. As a maintainer, I want the site's base path to stay outside the module, so that the dev server still reads it.
    32. As a maintainer, I want the page a walk is handed described once, in the module, so that the tests and the module cannot drift apart.
    33. As a maintainer, I want the harness to hold no lint suppressions, so that its functions are short enough to read and its constants say why they exist.
    34. As a maintainer, I want one layout-shift reading, so that a fix like #269's holds for every walk at once.
    35. As a builder of a real-use brief, I want a line in CODING_STANDARDS.md › Commands naming the walk, so that a brief can point at it instead of describing a driver.
    36. As the human, I want every browser case to have the same outcome before and after the move, so that the move changes where the code lives and nothing about what it checks.

    Implementation Decisions

    Rulings 1–7 and the settled list are on #182.

    • One deep module, the browser harness. It is declared in dependency-rules.md's Modules. Its entry is the one source file at the module folder's root (Spine's layout, as scripts/carry-assets has). The 34 files that name browser.mjs take the entry's new path. Every file stays at level infrastructure, so no ADR is needed.
    • What the module holds, private, in folders under the entry: the waits and the gestures, the Chrome finder, the static server with its two-piece send, the exit register, the browser walk, and the layout-shift reading. The site's base path stays outside the module.
    • The entry's interface: the browser walk, and chromePath. withBrowser and serve become private (ruling 6).
    • The browser walk takes a site (the built site, served for the walk, or a live address), a screen (desk 1280x900 or phone 390x844), and options carried over from today: watch the network, show scrollbars, errors expected, and a region whose shifts are marked. It hands the walker a page and a way to make the site's addresses. The walk returns the walker's result, the shifts of the page on screen when it ends (with that page's address), and every error of the walk (ruling 1, rulings 5 and 7).
    • The width check (ruling 3): after the first page draws, the walk reads innerWidth and fails, naming both widths, when it is not the screen's width. Emulation stays the way the width is set.
    • Errors (ruling 5): the walk keeps every error across its navigations and tabs, each with its address. It fails, listing them, when there is one, unless the caller says errors are expected. The tests' shared site opener says so. A tab's problems() keeps its meaning, and the counter's two local-only messages are still left out.
    • Shifts (rulings 2 and 7): one reading, moved from the tests into the module with #269's first-input rule. It is readable during a walk, and the walk applies it at its end. A caller may name a region whose shifts are marked. The tests' layout-shift helpers keep only what is theirs and are built on the module's reading. Nothing streams shifts from the browser.
    • Taps: tapping an element by selector, scrolled into view and then a real click, moves from the tests into the module.
    • Who moves (ruling 6): the tests' shared site opener, the 26 test files that serve and open a browser themselves, and the three deploy jobs all open the site through the walk. The asset renderer and the hand-run commands test take chromePath through the entry.
    • The page's description is written once, in the module, and the tests import that type.
    • Lint (ruling 4): withBrowser, its message handler and openTab come under 40 lines each, and the profile prefix gets its reason. The harness's entries leave eslint-suppressions.json.
    • Commands: CODING_STANDARDS.md › Commands gains a line saying that a live walk or a real-use check imports the browser walk from the harness's entry. Its Tests line, "Browser cases measure geometry and state from the running page, through scripts/browser.mjs", names the harness's entry instead, so the moved path is not left stale.
    • Bump: internal.

    Testing Decisions

    • A good test drives the harness through its entry, in real Chrome, over small fixture pages, and asserts what a walker sees: a failure's message, the errors returned, the shifts returned. It never reaches into the module's private files.
    • One seam, the entry (agreed 2026-10-28). The new cases, red before the walk exists:
    • Width: a phone walk over a page with no viewport meta makes Chrome report innerWidth 980, and the walk fails naming 390 and 980.
    • Errors: a page that throws fails the walk with the error listed. With errors expected, the same walk returns it.
    • Errors across pages: an error on the first page is still in the walk's errors after it navigates to a second.
    • Shifts: a page that shifts without input returns that shift, labelled with the page's address. A shift after a real tap is not counted.
    • The move has no new seam. Same-cases over the browser suites (Spine's same-cases.mjs) shows the same outcomes before and after, and the structure check is clean with the module declared.
    • Prior art: tests/browser.test.ts (the harness's waits over fixture pages in a real browser), tests/static-server.test.ts with tests/served-folder.ts (a served fixture folder), and tests/first-paint.test.ts (the shift reading and #269's tap case).

    Out of Scope

    • Claude in Chrome's own resize_window misreport (#217): that is the extension, not this harness.
    • Streaming every page's shifts to the harness (ruling 7).
    • A walk command-line tool: a walker writes a short script that imports the walk.
    • Changing any wait's or gesture's behaviour: they move unchanged.
    • Pull-request CI (#274).

    Further Notes

    • Real use: the session runs a browser walk on permitrulebook.com at both screens through the walk, and reports its width check, shifts and errors. The human has no step.
    • "Walk" in GLOSSARY.md names a person reading a flag. This spec says browser walk for the harness's walk, and the glossary gains no entry, because the harness is tooling, not the product's domain.
    • From the retros of #151, #167 and #208, and the architecture read at v1.2.3's close (card 2).

    Structure

    • module scripts/browser @infrastructure — the browser harness: the browser walk and the layout-shift reading, the tab's waits and gestures, Chrome found and driven over its protocol, the built site's static server, the exit register; its entry offers the browser walk and chromePath
    • edge scripts/smoke.mjs → scripts/browser — dependency
    • edge scripts/shot.mjs → scripts/browser — dependency
    • edge scripts/measure-taps.mjs → scripts/browser — dependency
    • edge scripts/render-assets.mjs → scripts/browser — dependency
    • edge scripts/browser → scripts/site-base.mjs — dependency
    • seam scripts/browser — production: headless Chrome over its protocol, on the built site served from dist/ or on the live site; test: fixture pages served from a temporary folder

    Tickets

    • #276 The browser harness becomes one declared module
    • #277 The browser harness holds no lint suppressions
    • #278 The browser walk opens a site at a screen and returns its shifts and errors
    • #279 The tests' shared site opener and 13 test files open the site through the browser walk
    • #280 The 13 sNN test files open the site through the browser walk
    • #281 Smoke, shot and measure-taps open the site through the browser walk
    • #282 Only the browser walk and chromePath leave the harness module

    #6 [new-need] The results screen has no door: ask for feedback at the moment the judgement happens

    closed without real-use check

    Reported by a reader through the maker (2026-09-10): the product should ask for feedback at some point — as a prompt that opens, or as an icon that is always there.

    Reported by a reader through the maker (2026-09-10): the product should ask for feedback at some point — as a prompt that opens, or as an icon that is always there.

    Where it stands today. The footer of every page carries "Report a wrong value" and "Suggest a route or a change", and a route page repeats the first one in its body, beside the data. The results screen — where a reader actually decides the product is wrong about them — carries neither in its body. So the moment the judgement happens is the moment with no door.

    What was tried and rejected. Two shapes were drawn in docs/spine/design/s7-feedback.html and the maker rejected both (2026-09-10):

    • A, a slip docked to the bottom edge — appears once after the results have been read, never dims the page, closable.
    • B, a centred modal over a dimmed page — the same words, but it stops the reading.

    Neither is the answer. Whatever replaces them has to keep the rules both were written under, because they are what make this product what it is:

    • it never appears before the reader has an answer, and never during the interview;
    • once, ever, remembered on the device;
    • it asks only for the two things the product can act on — a value that is wrong, a thing that should be different — with no rating, no e-mail field, and nothing leaving the device;
    • it says out loud that filing needs a GitHub account (see the sibling issue), because a link that ends at a login screen is a trap rather than a door;
    • it costs no tap target on a 390 px screen that the results already need.

    Not decided: whether the answer is a prompt at all. A quieter option is a line in the results screen's own body, in the page's voice, where the judgement happens — no furniture, no timing, no dismissal state.

    Wrong about you? A value that does not match its source, or something this screen should do — report a wrong value or suggest a change. Both open GitHub, where filing needs an account.

    It keeps every rule this issue set: it appears only where the reader has an answer to disagree with (a test asserts it is never rendered beside a question), it asks only for the two things the product can act on, nothing leaves the device, nothing is remembered, and the GitHub requirement is said before the click rather than discovered after it — #7 stays open, this only stops it surprising anyone.

    #7 [design-flaw] Every way back in needs a GitHub account

    closed without real-use check

    Every way back into this product ends at github.com, and filing there needs an account.

    Every way back into this product ends at github.com, and filing there needs an account.

    The tracker link on every page, the "Suggest a route or a change" link, and the route pages' "Report a wrong value" all open github.com/OytunOnal/permit-rulebook-data/issues/new/choose. A reader who is not a developer — which is most of the people this product is for, someone weighing a job offer with a non-EU passport — meets a sign-up wall at exactly the moment they were willing to help.

    Why it is still like this. The product has no backend by design: answers never leave the device, and a test asserts it. A form that posts a report needs somewhere to post it, and that is a server. So the cheapest door was the one that already existed.

    What the options cost, as far as they are understood today:

    • A `mailto:` link — no server, no account, works everywhere. Costs a public address that will be scraped, and a report that lands in a mailbox instead of a tracker with labels and history.
    • A hosted form (a third-party service) — no account for the reader, but a third party now receives what a reader types, which is a promise this product has not made and would have to make carefully; it also adds a connect-src/form-action exception to a policy that currently allows neither.
    • A tiny endpoint of our own — full control, and the first server this project has ever run: a deployment, a secret, an abuse surface, and a sentence in the privacy statement that today reads "there is no backend".
    • Leave it, and say so plainly — keep GitHub, but name the requirement at every door rather than letting a reader discover it after the click.

    Blocks nothing, but it caps everything: the feedback prompt in the sibling issue is worth little if the door behind it is locked.

    #9 [design-flaw] "Newest value read" is read as "last checked" — the label does not say which of two dates it is

    closed without real-use check

    Found by the product's own author on 2026-09-15, walking /data/: "footer da eski value'lar… Newest value read 2026-09-10 — bunlar dinamik değil mi?"

    Found by the product's own author on 2026-09-15, walking /data/: "footer da eski value'lar… Newest value read 2026-09-10 — bunlar dinamik değil mi?"

    They are dynamic, and they are right. The dataset holds 183 read dates; the newest is 2026-09-10 and dataset.json last changed that day (29fde08). Nothing in the dataset has changed since. The daily watch confirms every source unchanged and, by design, does not move a value's date when it does: the date beside a value is the day that reading was taken, and moving it on every confirmation would erase "unchanged since X". The day it was last confirmed is the line beside it — "re-read daily — last run 2026-09-15".

    The defect is the label. Two facts sit side by side — last changed 2026-09-10, last checked 2026-09-15 — and "Newest value read" says which one it is only to someone who already knows this product's meaning of "read". The author read it as "last checked". A label the product's own author misreads has not earned its meaning (the same class as s7's "ICT — seconded employee").

    Proposed fix, one page, two rows (src/lib/data-page.ts, the "What it holds today" facts list):

    • Newest value read 2026-09-10 → `Newest value changed 2026-09-10` — retrieved_at moves only when a person updates a value after a flag, which is a change, so the word is accurate.
    • a new row beneath it: `Last checked 2026-09-15`, from the watch's last_run — the fact the reader was looking for, with its own label.

    Left alone on purpose: the "read <date>" beside every quote, the RULES READ stamp, and the footer's "values read between … and …". There "read" means what it says — that sentence was taken from that page on that day — and the footer already prints the last run next to the span.

    Queued after s11 (which is merging today) and s10 (CLS, v1.1's last slice).

    #11 [design-flaw] Dataset JSON-LD: spatialCoverage as {"@type":"Country"} is "invalid object type" to Google

    closed without real-use check

    Source: Google Search Console → Datasets, export of 2026-09-16 (Non-critical issues.csv): Invalid object type for field "spatialCoverage", 1 item, validation not started. The dataset itself is valid (1 valid, 0 invalid, every day since 2026-09-11 — the first day Google saw /data/).

    Source: Google Search Console → Datasets, export of 2026-09-16 (Non-critical issues.csv): Invalid object type for field "spatialCoverage", 1 item, validation not started. The dataset itself is valid (1 valid, 0 invalid, every day since 2026-09-11 — the first day Google saw /data/).

    What we send (src/lib/dataset-ld.ts, live on /data/):

    "spatialCoverage": [{"@type":"Country","name":"Germany"}, …]

    Why it is flagged. In schema.org Country is a subtype of Place, so the markup is correct vocabulary — but Google's Dataset parser accepts spatialCoverage only as Text or `{"@type":"Place"}` (its three documented examples: a Place with GeoCoordinates, a Place with GeoShape, or a plain string such as "Tahoe City, CA"). Country is not on its list, hence "invalid object type". Non-critical: the dataset is still indexed and eligible; the property is simply dropped.

    Fix (one line, no copy change): emit the countries as text — spatialCoverage: countries (an array of the four names, or one joined string if the parser wants a single value) — or as {"@type":"Place","name":…}. The names come from dataset.countries, as today. tests/ has the JSON-LD case to extend: assert the type is text/Place, never Country.

    Verify: after the deploy, Search Console → Datasets → the issue's Validate fix; the Rich Results test on https://permitrulebook.com/data/ shows no warning on spatialCoverage.

    Not s13 (in flight); a slice of its own, small, or folded into site #10's /data/ pass.

  7. #299 Every page wears one frame, so the header stays put between pages and changes in one place

    specced from #142activev1.2.56 tickets, none merged yet

    Every page wears the same frame, the header, the footer and the menu, but each page draws it on its own, so a reader sees it shift between pages and a maintainer has to change it six times. The details:

    Problem Statement

    Every page wears the same frame, the header, the footer and the menu, but each page draws it on its own, so a reader sees it shift between pages and a maintainer has to change it six times. The details:

    • For a reader:
    • on the interview page the header and everything under it sit further out than on every other page, so the header jumps sideways on the first click away (v1.2.4 gate critique, finding 10);
    • on the data page the header's "The data" is not marked as the page you are on, though a country is marked on its pages and "Feedback" on its own (F7, F17, finding 11);
    • "Check yours" is not marked on the interview page either.
    • For a maintainer:
    • the six pages built as strings each retype the same frame: the head lines, the CSP, the icon links, the header, the footer, the menu script and the counter;
    • a change to the frame is six edits (#151's review touched every page file), and the frame has no test of its own;
    • three pages reach into the route page for its stylesheet, and every page reaches into the country page for the nav and the footer's facts;
    • the route page and the country page import each other.
    • The route page's own file is 1,071 lines against the 400-line limit:
    • it holds the page's composition, its rule cards, its rail, its statements, its notices, its figure, and one stylesheet carrying every page's rules;
    • its main function is 124 lines against 40;
    • five more page functions, the header and the footer pass 40 lines, and two test files pass 400. All of them are held today by ceilings and suppressions.

    Solution

    • One frame draws every page built as a string: route, country, data, feedback, 404 and the /status redirect. A page hands the frame its title, its preview lines, its own head lines, its own stylesheet, where it stands, and its content, and gets back the whole document.
    • The interview page, which Astro builds, takes its frame's pieces from the same module, and the body and column layout of the other pages. Its header then sits where every other page's does.
    • The frame marks the header item for the page it draws. "The data" is marked on the data page and "Check yours" on the interview page.
    • The route page becomes a module of its own, cut along what each part owns, with its stylesheet beside it.
    • Every page owns its own style rules; the frame keeps only its own and the blocks several pages share.
    • No function passes 40 lines, and no file or test file passes 400. The ceilings and suppressions that held them go.
    • Proof that a reader sees nothing else move:
    • every page kind's pixels are identical before and after;
    • every page's bytes are identical outside the stylesheet;
    • the only exceptions are the two marked header items, the interview page's layout, and two head lines that move below the CSP.

    User Stories

    1. As a reader moving from the interview to a route page, I want the header to stay where it was, so that the page does not seem to jump.
    2. As a reader on a phone, I want the interview page's side margins to match every other page's, so that the product feels like one site.
    3. As a reader on a wide screen, I want the interview's column to match the other pages' width, so that the wordmark and the nav sit in the same place on every page.
    4. As a reader on the data page, I want "The data" in the header marked as the page I am on, so that I know where I am, as I do on a country page or on the feedback page.
    5. As a reader on the interview page, I want "Check yours" marked as the page I am on, so that the header says where I am there too.
    6. As a screen reader user, I want the header's link to the page I am on to carry aria-current="page", so that I hear where I am.
    7. As a reader on a phone, I want the marked item to show in the opened menu as it does on a desktop, so that the mark is not desktop-only.
    8. As a reader, I want every route, country, data, feedback, 404 and status page to look exactly as it did, so that this work changes nothing I did not ask for.
    9. As a reader, I want the frame's links, its menu and the footer's facts to behave as before on every page, so that nothing I rely on breaks.
    10. As a maintainer, I want to change the header in one place, so that a change to the frame is one edit, not six.
    11. As a maintainer, I want the frame to have a test at its entry, so that a page that loses its header or its CSP fails a case.
    12. As a maintainer, I want a page to state only what differs (its title, preview lines, own head lines, stylesheet, place and content), so that a page file reads as that page.
    13. As a maintainer, I want no page to reach into another page for the stylesheet, the nav or the footer's facts, so that changing one page cannot break another.
    14. As a maintainer, I want the route page and the country page to stop importing each other, so that neither can be read only together with the other.
    15. As a maintainer, I want the route page split into its composition, its rule card, its rail, its statements, its notices and its figure, so that each part is one file I can read whole.
    16. As a maintainer, I want each page's style rules beside that page's code, so that a rule for route cards does not live in the frame.
    17. As a maintainer, I want the stylesheets read from .css files, the way the token set already is, so that style rules do not count against a code file's length.
    18. As a maintainer, I want every page function under 40 lines, so that each one reads as a composition of named parts.
    19. As a maintainer, I want the header and the footer under 40 lines each, so that the frame's own parts follow the same rule.
    20. As a maintainer, I want the route page's and the identity's test files under 400 lines, every case and helper under 40, so that a test file can be read whole.
    21. As a maintainer, I want the ceilings and suppressions for these files gone, so that the lint holds them to the rule like every other file.
    22. As a maintainer, I want the addresses the sitemap and the verdict read (the data page's and the feedback page's) to live in the site's address list, so that nothing outside the frame imports the frame for an address.
    23. As a maintainer, I want the seal, the stamps and the "Rules read" stamp to stay the identity's, so that a page's masthead and the interview's masthead keep drawing them without reaching into the frame.
    24. As a maintainer, I want the frame and the route page declared as modules, so that the structure check holds their entries and their private files.
    25. As a reviewer, I want the frame's word, Frame, in the glossary, so that the code and the review use one word for it.
    26. As a reviewer, I want a proof that every built page's bytes outside the stylesheet are unchanged, except the named exceptions, so that I can trust the move moved nothing.
    27. As a reviewer, I want a proof that every page kind's pixels are unchanged at 390 px and at desktop width in both colour schemes, so that moving the style rules changed nothing a reader sees.
    28. As a reviewer, I want the route page's existing cases to keep their names and outcomes across the split, so that the split is proven by the tests that were already there.
    29. As a reviewer, I want the route-page fingerprint regenerated once, with the reason in the commit, so that its change is on purpose and stated.
    30. As the human at the merge, I want the interview page's before and after screenshots, so that I can judge the one page whose layout moves.

    Implementation Decisions

    The rulings behind each decision are on #142 (rulings 1–10, 2026-10-30), with the notes in ruling 10.

    The frame module (rulings 1, 2, 4, 5)

    • A new deep module, `frame`, declared among the modules, every file at the presentation level.
    • Its entry is named for its main export, framedPageHtml, which returns a whole page's document.
    • It pairs with the copy's frame file, which already holds the frame's words.
    • It draws the six pages built as strings: route, country, data, feedback, 404 and the /status redirect.
    • What a page hands the frame. The shape is the grill's, ruling 4:
      framedPageHtml(dataset, {
    title,
    meta?,      // { description, path, kind }: link previews; 404 and status have none
    headTags?,  // the page's own head lines: data's ld+json, 404's robots, status's refresh
    css?,       // the page's own rules
    place?,     // where it stands: marks the header and footer, and gives the footer's JSON and check links
    run?,       // the watch run the footer reports
    content,    // everything between the header and the footer, masthead included
    scripts?,   // beyond the menu: feedback's copy script
  })
    • The masthead and `<main>` are the page's, inside content, because their markup differs between pages.
    • The page's own head lines sit right after the CSP line. So the 404's and the status page's robots, refresh and canonical lines move one place down, below the CSP.
    • Private inside the frame:
    • the header, the footer and the menu script, which leave the identity file;
    • the CSP;
    • the icon links;
    • the countries' nav links and the footer's facts, which leave the country page;
    • the frame's stylesheet.
    • The entry also exports `interviewFrameOf(dataset)` for the interview page. It returns that page's pieces, { policy, icons, header, footer, menuScript }, and its Astro head places them.
    • The identity file keeps the identity marks: the seal, the stamps and the "Rules read" stamp. The frame reads the seal for the wordmark.
    • The site's address list takes the data page's and the feedback page's paths.
    • Import directions:
    • the nav links are built from the dataset's countries and the slug functions, never from the country page, so the frame imports no page;
    • the frame reads only the site's addresses, the identity marks, the slugs, the escaping functions, the frame's words, and, for the CSP's hashes, the first-paint and clipboard scripts;
    • the cycle between the route page and the country page goes.

    Style (rulings 3, 9)

    • The shared page stylesheet leaves the route page:
    • the frame keeps its own rules (tokens, base, column, tap, masthead, the identity stylesheet) and the blocks several pages share (.cta, .data, .src);

    • The body and column layout moves into the identity stylesheet, which the interview page already links, and the interview's stylesheet drops its own:
    • it is the string pages' layout: a 56rem column whose 1.3rem side padding sits inside it, and 1.6rem above the header;
    • on the interview page only, the column narrows by about 42 px at desktop width, each gutter widens by about 6 px at 390 px, and the header moves up by 1.2rem;
    • the interview's scrollbar-gutter stays its own (s31).

    The current page (ruling 8)

    • The frame marks the header item for the page it draws, from place: "The data" on the data page, "Feedback" as now, a country on its pages, and "Check yours" on the interview page through interviewFrameOf.

    The route page module (ruling 6)

    • A new deep module, `route-page`, every file at the presentation level.
    • Its entry exports:
    • routePage and routePages;
    • what the country and data pages read: audienceSentence, gist, pageStamp, routeFigure.

    routePage falls under 40 lines by composing a masthead, a main and an aside.

    • Private files:
    • the rule card: heading, kind, plain line, quote and asks box;
    • the rail: the threshold rail;
    • the stated blocks: statements, carve-outs and unsourced lines;
    • the notices: the notices, the read stamp and the unread sources;
    • the route figure: the answer block's figure and the gist;
    • the page's own stylesheet.
    • The copy's route-page file keeps the page's words.

    Lengths (ruling 7)

    • countryPage, dataPage, feedbackPage, notFoundPage and datasetLd each come in at most 40 lines, and so do the header and the footer inside the frame.
    • The route page's and the identity's test files come in at most 400 lines, every case and helper at most 40.

    Helpers written more than once (ruling 12)

    • Frame is added: what every page of the site carries around its own content, the same on every page: the head, the header, the footer and the menu.

    Bump (ruling 10): Z, internal. The visible fixes add no promise. No ADR: no level moves.

    Testing Decisions

    A good test here drives a seam and reads what it returns or what the browser draws: a page's document, a measured box, a screenshot's pixels. It does not read a file's source, and it does not import a private file.

    • The frame's entry (new).
    • A test file drives framedPageHtml and interviewFrameOf. It checks:
    • the frame is present on every page: the CSP, the icon links, the header, the footer and the menu script;
    • aria-current is on each header destination's own page and nowhere else;
    • a page's css, headTags and scripts land where the interface puts them.
    • Cases that call the header, the footer, the CSP's hash function or the nav links directly move here, or read the built pages, because those become private.
    • Each page's builder (existing): routePage, countryPage, dataPage, feedbackPage and notFoundPage.
    • Their cases keep their names and outcomes across the split, proven by same-cases on the commits that move code.
    • The two long test files are cut along the same seams.
    • The built site in Chrome (existing, the `withSite` walk).
    • The header's measured case today leaves position out. It gains the wordmark's left edge and top, compared between the interview page and a route page at 390 px and at desktop width, under device emulation.
    • Screenshots of the marked item's red underline on the data page and on the interview page, at 390 px with the menu open and at desktop width, in both colour schemes, each set explicitly.
    • One-off proof (`.run/`, as #184's).
    • Every built page's bytes outside <style>, before and after, identical but for the named exceptions: the two marked header items, and the 404's and status page's head lines below the CSP.
    • Full-page screenshots of each page kind before and after, at 390 px and at desktop width, in both colour schemes, identical in pixels but for the marked items and the interview page.
    • The route-page fingerprint changes once, when the stylesheet moves. Its fixture is regenerated on purpose, with the reason in the commit.
    • Prior art:
    • the header's measured case and the CSP's every-page case;
    • the route page's fingerprint over the frozen dataset;
    • #184's composed-verdicts proof under .run/.

    Out of Scope

    • Drawing the interview page through `framedPageHtml`. Astro keeps its head, which carries the first-paint script and style (ruling 1).
    • Making the masthead one markup. Route, 404 and status draw a ruled <header>, while country, data and feedback draw a plain <div>. Both stay the page's own.
    • Making the footer mark the page it is on, beyond a country as today.
    • Any change of words. The copy is untouched.

    Structure

    • module src/lib/frame @presentation — the frame every page built as a string wears, and the interview page's pieces of it; its entry framed-page.ts
    • module src/lib/route-page @presentation — one route page, its rule cards, rail, statements, notices and figure; its entry route-page.ts
    • edge src/lib/route-page → src/lib/frame — dependency
    • seam src/lib/frame — production: the route, country, data, feedback, 404 and status pages through framedPageHtml, the interview page through interviewFrameOf; test: the frame's entry case driving both

    Bet: one check in the walk catches what 70 hand checks miss, and no case turns red for a reason that is not a real error.

    From the architecture read at v1.2.4's close (card 1, strong; card 3, worth exploring, folded in), placed on the human's word, 2026-10-28, with no milestone; the re-plan places it. The read's report: .run/architecture-v1.2.4/architecture-review.html.

    What a maintainer sees

    • walkSite already fails on every page's and every tab's error, each with its address. But withSite (tests/browser-walk.ts, imported by 41 test files) passes errorsExpected: true, which turns that off.
    • In its place, 22 test files assert page.problems() by hand, 70 times (checked 2026-10-28).
    • problems() reads this tab's errors since its last navigation (scripts/browser/tab/tab-page.mjs:32). So an error on any page but the last passes unseen.
    • tests/s27.test.ts:411-415 stitches two pages' lists by hand across a goto to work around it.
    • tests/orientation.test.ts:345 reads allProblems(), filtered for a CSP refusal.
    • #275's ruling 5 kept errorsExpected so the move changed no outcome. This is the step after it, not a reversal.

    The proposed fix

    1. The walk owns the check.
    2. withSite and the test walks drop errorsExpected. A case that expects an error (the walk's own cases, orientation's CSP read) reads Walked.errors.
    3. problems() and allProblems() leave BrowserPage, and the 70 hand asserts go.
    4. Smoke and shot keep errorsExpected, since they word the errors in their reports.
    5. The beacon-noise rule moves to the walk's log. isLocalBeaconNoise moves from tab/tab-events.mjs to walk/walk-log.mjs, its one reader once TabEvents keeps no list.
    6. Card 3: the tab is a module of its own.
    7. Declare scripts/browser/tab in docs/roadkeeper/dependency-rules.md's ## Modules, with open-tab.mjs as its entry, re-exporting the BrowserPage and SentRequest types.
    8. Rerun the structure command. After step 2, walk/ reaches tab/ only through its entry.
    9. Without it, the next walk part (a second gesture, a frame tab) could build TabWaits or TabGestures itself and skip the first-input wait #269 settled, and the check would say nothing.

    Land it before #198, which splits several of the same files (s19, s25–s27, s30, record, orientation). A page that logs an error on an intermediate step turns red here first: that is the point, and each such red is a bug to name, not a case to loosen.

    Done when

    • No test walk passes errorsExpected except smoke and shot, and no test calls problems() or allProblems().
    • A throwaway case that throws on a first page and navigates on is red, naming that page's address (once, by hand, in the build report).
    • ## Modules names scripts/browser/tab with its entry, and the structure check reads it as a deep module nested in scripts/browser, clean.

    #82 — core.ts reads as a binary file: a raw NUL in sliceFingerprint

    Repository: permit-rulebook-data.

    Problem. src/watch/core.ts (about 1260 lines) has a raw U+0000 byte at sliceFingerprint:

    sha256(`${entry.slice.from}<NUL>${entry.slice.to}`)

    A NUL is a good separator, since no slice text can contain one. But because the byte is raw, ripgrep treats the whole file as binary. rg cutExcerpt src/watch finds the caller in run-says.ts but not the definition, and the architecture review's own searches missed it. Any search of the watch's largest file needs grep -a.

    Proposed fix (architecture review at the close of v1.2.0, card 4, "Strong"):

    • Write the separator as the escape \0 (${entry.slice.from}\0${entry.slice.to}), with a comment saying why it is a NUL.
    • The escape yields the same character, so every slice_read fingerprint in watch/state.json stays byte-identical, and no re-baseline follows.

    Done when:

    • core.ts holds no raw control byte, and ripgrep searches it as text.
    • A case shows that a fingerprint taken before the change is unchanged.

    One character; it fits in any pull request on the data repository.

    Line as of data `34c358d`: `src/watch/core.ts:286`.

The package runs in the site's build and in the reader's browser. None is exploitable: the one attacker is a contributor's pull request, and the owner reviews and merges it. They share one concern and one kind of fix, so they are one issue.

    From the Security read of the launch code (#25, 2026-10-19), ruled later by the human. These are five breaches of CODING_STANDARDS.md ## Security in the data package. The package runs in the site's build and in the reader's browser. None is exploitable: the one attacker is a contributor's pull request, and the owner reviews and merges it. They share one concern and one kind of fix, so they are one issue.

    • C — `watch/state.json` is never validated.
    • Where: src/watch/state.ts:199-216 (data), and the site's src/lib/site.ts:262, which casts it to WatchState.
    • What: snapshot.retrieved_at reaches the site's <time datetime>. state.entries[entry.id] also finds inherited keys: an id of constructor gives last_read undefined.
    • Fix: a state schema (a date pattern on retrieved_at), checked in unreadSources, and lookups through Object.hasOwn.
    • D — `data/countries.json` has no schema.
    • Where: src/countries.ts:39, which casts it with as CountryVocabulary.
    • What: code, name, article, adjective and aliases are unchecked strings, and they reach option labels and the unread sentence.
    • Fix: a schema (code ^[A-Z]{2}$, length-capped strings), compiled inside validateDataset.

    • What: «\s*([^»]+?)\s*» backtracks polynomially over every dataset text. The schema caps only summary (maxLength 600): no other string has a maxLength, and no array a maxItems.

    • F — unbounded depth.
    • Where: schema/ruleset.schema.json:934-939, and the walks at engine.ts:317 (evalCriterion), :840 (forEachCriterion), :265 (referencedFields), validate.ts:128 and prose.ts:183.
    • What: an any path's criteria refers back to criterion, so disjunctions nest without limit, and every walk recurses without a depth bound.
    • Fix: forbid any inside a path, or cap the depth in semanticErrors.
    • G — `data/exclusions.md` is unbounded and its twin has no schema.
    • Where: src/exclusions.ts:45-66.
    • What: the file is split and matched with no length cap, and the twin's route and limb ids are free text.
    • Fix: cap the length; hold the twin ids to the route and limb id patterns.

  4. #222 The analytics beacon runs as a pinned copy with its integrity hash

    What becomes possible: the analytics beacon follows Spine's general rule "A third-party script is pinned to a version and loaded with its integrity hash" (SPINE_STANDARDS.md, Security), so the product needs no departure from it, and a change on Cloudflare's side cannot change the script our pages run.

    What becomes possible: the analytics beacon follows Spine's general rule "A third-party script is pinned to a version and loaded with its integrity hash" (SPINE_STANDARDS.md, Security), so the product needs no departure from it, and a change on Cloudflare's side cannot change the script our pages run.

    Why now: PR #219 moved this product's general rules into Spine's SPINE_STANDARDS.md. Today the beacon is the one exception: src/lib/site.ts loads https://static.cloudflareinsights.com/beacon.min.js, unversioned and with no integrity hash, and the Content-Security-Policy allows it by name. The human ruled to follow the rule wherever the product can, rather than write a departure (2026-10-24): "kurallara uyabildiğin noktada uy. gereksiz departure ekleme".

    The bet: Cloudflare Web Analytics counts a page view sent by a pinned copy of its beacon, served from our own origin with its integrity hash, just as it counts one sent by the script it serves. If it does not, the departure comes back with that evidence.

    What to build

    • The beacon is a copy of a named version, committed or carried at build time, loaded with its integrity hash.
    • The Content-Security-Policy no longer allows static.cloudflareinsights.com. It still allows the reports to cloudflareinsights.com/cdn-cgi/rum.
    • CODING_STANDARDS.md's Content-Security-Policy line names what the pages run after the change.

    Done when

    • A page view on the live site shows in Cloudflare Web Analytics with the pinned copy. That needs the human's dashboard.
    • A test proves every script the pages load is our own, or pinned with its hash.

  2. #150 One command removes a worktree: junction first, branches proven in their base

    From the retro of #133 (comment on #97, 2026-10-21), seen before in #110's; opened on the human's word.

    From the retro of #133 (comment on #97, 2026-10-21), seen before in #110's; opened on the human's word.

    What the session does by hand

    A site worktree holds node_modules\permit-rulebook-data, a junction to the sibling data checkout. Removing the worktree with the junction in place deletes the data repository's own files through it. So after every merge the session does, by hand: remove the junction alone (cmd //c rmdir "<wt>\node_modules\permit-rulebook-data"), recount the links, check that permit-rulebook-data/package.json still exists, remove the worktree, prove each branch it held is in its base, and delete those branches locally and on origin. Six times in #133.

    Done when

    • npm run worktree:remove -- <path> [<base>] does those steps in that order, and refuses while any junction or symbolic link under the worktree remains.
    • It checks that the data repository's package.json exists before and after, and stops if it does not.
    • It deletes only branches proven in <base> (default master), locally and on origin, and names each branch it kept and why.
    • Tested against a scratch worktree with a junction to a scratch target: the target survives, a branch not in its base is kept.

    Folds in

    From the retro of #151 (comment on #97, 2026-10-22), seen before in the retros of #110 and #133; folded on the human's word. The setup half: #151's build hand-wrote setup-151.mjs (a data worktree and a site worktree side by side, both installed, the data built, the site's file:../permit-rulebook-data link checked), used for nine tickets, the merge folder and the fix round, and a later check built two more pairs by hand.

    • npm run worktree:add -- <name> <base> [--detach] makes wt-<name> with a data worktree and a site worktree side by side, on a branch <base>-<name> from origin/<base> in each (or detached at it), installs both, builds the data, and checks that the site's permit-rulebook-data resolves to the data worktree beside it; it stops if the folder exists.
    • worktree:remove takes the same <name> and removes both worktrees and both branches by the steps above.
    • Tested with worktree:remove's scratch case: a pair added, then removed, the target data repository's package.json intact.

    #81 — The stand-in belongs to its cover

    Repository: this one (the site).

    Problem. The glossary defines a stand-in as the line shown in the covered place until the cover comes off. Since #67 the cover has one owner (src/lib/first-paint.ts), but its stand-in still has four:

    • COVERS knows the stand-in only as a class name (uncovers.standIn), and STAND_IN_RULES styles it.
    • src/lib/question.ts (renderStandInsOverQuestionOne, holdLineHtml) writes its markup and spells the same class names again.
    • src/lib/copy.ts holds its words (RETURNING_LINE, LINK_ARRIVAL_LINE).
    • src/pages/index.astro paints the stand-ins, removes them with querySelectorAll(".stand-in"), and styles .stand-in-verdict in its own <style>.

    The class name is the seam, and it is spelled by hand on both sides. A test on the rendered string is what keeps the four spellings equal, and a fourth cover takes four edits.

    Proposed fix (architecture review at the close of v1.2.0, card 2, "Worth exploring"):

    • COVERS carries each stand-in's line.
    • first-paint.ts renders the stand-ins from the set (markup and stylesheet both). takeCoversOff removes cover and stand-ins in the one task that draws the reader's first screen.
    • question.ts draws question one and nothing of the first paint.
    • index.astro loses its .stand-in selector and its .stand-in-verdict style.

    Done when:

    • A new cover with its stand-in is one entry in the set.
    • The pairing of cover and stand-in is a property of the set, tested through it, not through a rendered string.
    • No first-paint behaviour moves: every arrival still holds still.

    Lines are as of site `4136be3`: `src/lib/question.ts` 188–206; `src/pages/index.astro` 67 and 122 (render), 245 (removal), 1787 (style). Report: `.run/architecture-review-2026-10-18-v1.2.0.html` (git-ignored).

  3. #96 A route page's headline prints each read date as large as the figure it dates

    Found in the real use of #76 (#79), on the live site on 2026-10-19.

    Found in the real use of #76 (#79), on the live site on 2026-10-19.

    What a reader sees

    Since #76, every route page's headline panel ends each figure with its own read date. That date is printed as large as the figure itself: 24 px bold mono, while the figure's label beside it is 12 px.

    • On a phone (390 px), `/spain/eu-blue-card/`: "· read 2026-09-04" sits in large bold type at the end of the first figure's label, directly above "€41,356.36/year", and reads like a third headline value. On the second figure the "•" is left at the end of one line, and "read 2026-09-02" drops alone onto the next line in large type.
    • On a desktop, `/germany/experienced-worker/`: "· read 2026-09-02" wraps onto its own line under "€45,630/year", at the figure's size.

    Which figure a date belongs to can still be told from the order, so #79's check 3 passed on its words. The date's weight is the defect: it competes with the amount it dates.

    Why

    headlineFigures (src/lib/route-page.ts) puts the <time> after the answer-label span, inside p.answer-figure. That rule sets font: 600 1.5rem var(--font-mono), and nothing styles the time, so it inherits the figure's size. Before #76 the panel's date sat in the small sentence under the figures.

    Done when

    • A figure's read date is set like its label (the label's size and colour from tokens.css), on the same line as the label where it fits.
    • The separator never sits alone at a line's end: it stays with the date it introduces.
    • At 390 and at 1920, on a route with one figure, two figures and points, the amount is the only large thing in the panel.
    • The first paint still holds still, and every tap target is still 44 px at 390.

    #85 later rewrites what the date says ("first read … · confirmed unchanged …"). This issue is only how large it is, so it does not wait for #85.

    #58 — A page shell, and the two import cycles go with it

    Repository: this one (the site).

    Problem. Six documents are assembled by hand — src/lib/route-page.ts 700–811, country-page.ts 167–262, data-page.ts 84–260 and 273–315, feedback-page.ts ~100–199, not-found.ts 50–95, and src/pages/index.astro 81–140 — each repeating the doctype, contentSecurityPolicy(), iconLinks(), the head meta, siteHeader(navCountries(dataset)), siteFooter(…, footerFacts(…)), MENU_SCRIPT and the beacon. The shared parts live in whichever page grew them first: PAGE_CSS in route-page.ts (imported by data-page, feedback-page, not-found), footerFacts and navCountries in country-page.ts (imported by five modules). So pages import each other, and two pairs are import cycles today: country-page ↔ route-page and data-page ↔ dataset-ld. One concept, the provenance line (quote, host, read day, official link), has two implementations — card.ts provenanceHtml (387) and route-page.ts quoteBlock (278) — under the same class names .src and .rail, styled differently in two stylesheets (index.astro 2090/2123, route-page.ts 894/910).

    Deepening. One page-shell module returns the full document for a place (which page, its title, its extra head) and owns the shared CSS, the header, the footer facts and the policy; each page supplies only its body.

    Wins. A header, footer or CSP change touches one module; the two cycles go, which the structure check (#37) would otherwise report first; identity.test, footer.test and csp.test can test the shell once instead of reading every built page.

    Evidence. f8737da, d77471d and cb9d042 each touched six page files; f6b9a37 rewrote contentSecurityPolicy([MENU_SCRIPT]) in every shell.

    Done when no page imports another page, every document comes from the shell, and the provenance line has one implementation.

    Raised by the architecture review of 2026-10-17 (`/improve-codebase-architecture`, scoped by the last 300 commits of both repositories); filed on the human's word to take every candidate. Line numbers are as of site `9f4d6c8` and data `1cb26e8`.

    Folds in

  5. #145 A kept issue reaches no one: it is opened by a bot and neither assigns nor mentions the owner

    Repository: OytunOnal/permit-rulebook-data (the kept-issue CLI), and the workflows that call it in both repositories.

    Repository: OytunOnal/permit-rulebook-data (the kept-issue CLI), and the workflows that call it in both repositories.

    Found by #125's real use (real use of #117), 2026-10-21; opened on the human's word.

    What the human sees

    Today three red runs that nobody watched kept their issues as #117 promised: #140 deploy run failed opened, data#40 check failed on master opened, data#31 watch run failed gained a comment. None of it reached the human. Their GitHub notifications for the day hold only GitHub Actions' own "… workflow run failed for master branch" entries (the ci_activity kind that #65 found "went out all ten days and changed nothing"), and nothing for #140, data#40 or data#31. The issues are opened and commented on by github-actions[bot], and a thread the human neither takes part in nor is mentioned in does not notify them.

    Why it matters

    #117 exists so that a red run nobody watches reaches someone. A kept issue that only waits to be found keeps #65's ten silent days possible.

    Done when

    • When the kept-issue CLI opens or reopens a kept issue, it assigns it to the repository's owner; each red comment @mentions the owner. The owner comes from the run's own context, never typed into the code.
    • A green run's closing line mentions no one.
    • Tested through the action the module decides and the exact gh argument lists it sends (ghArgumentsOf), as the kept-issue suites do today.
    • On the next real red, the human's notifications hold the kept issue itself (reason assign or mention), read by the session, not asked.

    #18 Permanent residence

    Planned in the ledger: wave 2 (v2).

    Planned in the ledger: wave 2 (v2).

    Permanent residence (v2 candidate, human's idea 2026-09-11: "permanent residency ve vatandaşlık yollarını da eklesek mi") · why: same reader, same journey, later step; and the rules are the shape this engine already handles — years, language level, income, no benefits · what it needs first, and it is not small: a history. Every PR rule keys on years of lawful residence under a particular status, and which status changes the count — study years often count half or not at all, a Blue Card shortens the track, Türkiye's Decision 1/80 runs on its own clock. Today the interview asks only where the reader stands now; PR turns a snapshot into a timeline, which is a new question set and a new engine concept · and it changes what a verdict is: work permits say "you meet this today", PR says "you will, on this path, in N years" — a projection, which is a much stronger claim than this product has ever made and a more harmful one to get wrong · bets A17 and A18: the timeline is worth building because the dated-and-quoted promise is worth more across a journey than across one step · gate: one country, one PR route, measured end to end before a second is opened.

#206 Delete the Cloudflare Pages preview project

waiting for 7 days

Why it is yours: the Cloudflare dashboard needs your Cloudflare login, and no tool here can sign in to it.

What and why

The per-branch preview on Cloudflare Pages is no longer used. #199's fix round deletes its setup doc (docs/spine/preview.md) and its build script (scripts/preview-build.sh), on your ruling of 2026-10-23 (comment on #199). Once the script is gone, every branch push would make the Cloudflare project fail its build, so the project goes too.

Steps

  1. Open https://dash.cloudflare.com → Compute (Workers & Pages).
  2. Look for a Pages project named `permit-rulebook`. It is connected to Git for OytunOnal/permit-rulebook, its production branch is preview-only, and its build command is bash scripts/preview-build.sh.
  3. Open it → Settings → at the bottom, Delete project, and confirm with its name.
  4. Optional: at https://github.com/settings/installations, the Cloudflare Workers and Pages app. If OytunOnal/permit-rulebook was its only repository, uninstall it; otherwise remove that repository from its list.

Pass

The Workers & Pages list has no permit-rulebook project. https://permit-rulebook.pages.dev no longer serves the site; Cloudflare answers with its own not-found page.

If it fails

  • No such project: it was never set up, or was already removed. Comment "no project" and close this issue.
  • Delete is refused, for example because a custom domain is attached: comment with Cloudflare's message, and leave this open. permitrulebook.com itself is served by GitHub Pages and must not be detached from there.

Note: from this machine permit-rulebook.pages.dev resolves to ::1 and an address that times out, so the project's state could not be checked from here.
