Levels and modules

docs/roadkeeper/dependency-rules.md · docs/roadkeeper/structure.json

  • 8 modules, and 83 files outside any module
  • No dependencies on an outer level
  • Not drawn: 488 dependencies leaving the code read; 61 declarations over the page's cap; 4 declared relations naming no drawn module
What the marks mean
  • Bands are the levels, outermost on top. Two levels in one band, drawn with a | between them, may not use each other.
  • A module spans the bands its files and nested modules are in. The line down a module's left edge is solid beside each level the module has files on, and dashed beside a level it only passes through, with no files there.
  • A file outside any module is a box of its own in its level's band.
  • + − «type»: an exported name, a private one, a type: UML's marks.
  • 1 of 12 reached: the files code outside the module uses; a deep module's is 1, its entry. The bar under it shows the share.
  • past the interface: files code outside reaches around the entry, red on the bar.
  • shallow?: a module whose only file is its entry.
  • Several root files: a module with more than one root file has no entry; the check reports them, and the module is drawn red.
  • cycle: a tag on a module's box when it and other modules use one another in a loop; hover the tag for them.
  • A file on several levels spans their bands: red, or orange when an exception covers it.
  • An arrow stands for the dependencies between two boxes; hover or select it for how many. It leaves at the band most of them start in, and enters where most end.
  • Red, outward: a dependency on an outer level, or on the other level of its band; orange: an exception covers it, until its review point; grey: inward.
  • A dashed arrow: a dependency on types only; a triangle head: implements or inherits.
  • 17 dependencies inside: what a module's box hides between its own files.
  • used by 5 · depends on 2: a file box's dependencies, the ones on it and the ones from it.
  • A chip on a box's edge, inside a module: what the box uses outside the view; +N more when they do not fit.
  • A declared relation: a line with UML's marks, a diamond for an aggregation or a composition, an open head otherwise.

docs/roadkeeper/ARCHITECTURE.md

ARCHITECTURE — Permit Rulebook (as of v1, public and announced 2026-09-09)

Updated at every slice exit. Three diagrams, one question each: where the facts come from, how they become a site, where the reader's answers stay. Labels are names; what each name means is in the list below the diagrams.

1 · Data flow — where the facts come from

flowchart LR
    Sources -->|fetch, hash| Watch --> Flags
    Flags -.->|a person edits| Dataset
    Dataset --> Gates
    Exclusions --> Gates

2 · Pipeline — how the facts become a site

flowchart LR
    Lock -->|which data commit| Build
    Dataset --> Build
    Engine --> Build
    Tokens --> Build
    Build --> Dist --> CI --> Pages
    Watch -->|dataset-updated| CI

3 · Trust boundary — where the answers stay

flowchart LR
    subgraph web["permitrulebook.com"]
        Pages
    end
    subgraph device["The reader's device"]
        RoutePage["Route page"]
        Interview
        Record
    end
    Pages --> RoutePage
    Pages --> Interview
    RoutePage -->|"check yours"| Interview
    Interview --> Record
    Interview -.->|"report a wrong value"| Tracker

Nothing crosses the boundary from the device outward except a reader's own click on the tracker link. Answers never leave the device.

The names

Diagram 1 — permit-rulebook-data (sibling repository; data CC BY 4.0, code MIT)

  • Sources — the official pages and PDFs: ZAV, BOE, UGE, IND, service-public.gouv.fr, europa.eu, efta.int, buzer.
  • Watch — the daily re-read (src/watch, GitHub Actions): strategies html, pdf-text (embedded-font text layer, bytes hash beside words hash) and link liveness; slices bind each page to its operative text; glyph corrections are declared data; human_tier: 2 since 2026-09-10 (two sources a browser reads and this fetcher cannot — see the glossary); runs daily in GitHub Actions and, after its state is pushed, files an issue (source-change) per flag this run created or changed; a flag still open on the second UTC morning after it was raised turns the run red and is named in one issue the run keeps, overdue flags (#62). A red run on master keeps watch run failed, and the first green one closes it (#117). Every kept issue is decided in one module, kept-issue, and carried to the tracker by one CLI, built on its own so a broken build cannot silence it, that runs gh with no shell (#117). Two readers, a fetcher and a browser (Chrome over its own protocol), and the coverage gate ask one module, trust-line, where the watch may go: the entry address, a redirect target, every address a name resolves to (the fetcher's; a name Chrome resolves for itself is the stated gap) and the page a reader lands on. It imports only the failure wording; the fetcher keeps only HTTP (#104). What a finished run says (its flags, its log lines and its exit code) is decided in one module, run-says; the CLI only reads, prints and writes (#72). It audits every installed dependency first; a known advisory at high or above turns the run red at its end and stops none of its reading (#24).
  • Flags — one file per change, with the page's excerpt in a fenced code block so nothing in it acts on the issue, and every line around it ours (#72); walked by a person, who edits the dataset or records what was found, within two days.
  • Dataset — data/dataset.json: 29 routes in 4 countries, 23 of them asked about and 6 quoted only; every numeric value with its source URL, verbatim quote, retrieval date and append-only history; per route its statements (preconditions and caveats in the source's words), its readings (ours, declared) and a scope value with the limbs it does not ask. A question whose options are rungs of one amount is marked ordered; a criterion with paths and each path carry a label; a question names a route only through a {route:<id>} slot, filled with the route's what_it_is (#151). A path answer someone else arranges (a transfer, a hosting agreement) is marked is_arranged, and only the path question may carry the mark (schema 0.8.3, #167). Beside it data/countries.json (199 passport issuers, labels, aliases, the article a name takes; classes.eu_eea_ch is a rule with four sourced legs; and 11 territories, none a row, each with the passport its people hold and an official sentence that says so) and schema/ruleset.schema.json, the public contract.
  • Reader's words from the data — the data package composes the words the site prints from the dataset: a country's name with its article, at a sentence's start and as a possessive; the scope line in two forms (where the reader has answered, "checked against your answers"; where not, "the checker asks about it"); a {place} filled "in <country>" or "in the country you move to"; and which kind of host a source is on, authority or consolidated text (#151). The site holds the labels; the package holds the facts.
  • Exclusions — data/exclusions.md: what was researched and left out, by route, as prose plus a fenced machine twin.
  • Gates — npm run check: schema and semantic validation · watch coverage both ways · quote fidelity (every shipped quote found in its snapshot) · prose provenance (every renderable sentence is authority, ours or label, keyed on the declared kind) · every route and notice source, and every learn link, on an https host on the authority list or the consolidated-text list · labels on paths · words on an ordered range · route names only in slots · each territory's passport on the list with an https source (#151) · the arranged mark only on the path question (#167). A failing gate fails the build downstream. The data repository runs them on every push to master, every pull request and after every watch run (check.yml); a red check after a watch run keeps check failed on master, and the next green one closes it (#117).

Diagram 2 — permit-rulebook (this repository; MIT)

  • Engine — pure functions in the data package: eligibility by eq/in/gte/points/any, band edges = thresholds, deciding path, still-reachable, points as the best row an answer satisfies, questions by information gain, provable single-step unlocks, notices; property tests over thousands of generated profiles. A disjunction is judged path by path in its own module (src/disjunction.ts): it is a hard fail only when no path is open, every open path asks its questions, and when every path failed the deciding path is the nearest gap or else the open path with the fewest unmet rules. reckonAskingRoutes names, from the same walk as the asking rule, the routes a question is asked for and the open ones; questions-do-work checks, per destination and per rung, that an answer moves some route's decision (#133). isStepGated decides which routes wait on a step; routesAJobOfferFrees counts, per country, the routes a job offer would free for a reader with none, the job offer itself decided once by findJobOfferAnswer (#179); a gap is said once, exact and with its period, and a band open at the bottom names the line it is under (#167).
  • Tokens — tokens.css (the design system) and identity.css (the identity pair: the tilted PR stamp over the read-date stamp; one source, inlined by the route page, linked by the interview).
  • Build — Astro, base derived from SITE_URL, the site's address, which is one literal line in pages.yml: the deploy reads no repository variable (#110). An invalid dataset breaks the build; the social card is rendered from the dataset's own facts with a sidecar that makes a stale card fail CI.
  • Dist — 38 pages (the interview, /data/, /feedback/, the status page, the 404, 4 country pages, 29 route pages generated from the dataset, never typed) plus 29 route JSON endpoints, the dataset and the countries as JSON, the sitemap, favicons, the social card.
  • CI — pages.yml: both repositories checked out, data gates, build, tests with a real browser over dist/, the lint, asset truth, base-path check, tap targets at 390 px, the carry, then deploy. The lint (eslint.config.mjs) loads Roadkeeper's preset from roadkeeper-lint/, which holds the limits, 400 lines a file and 40 a function with every line counted. The files over 400 lines are Ceilings in docs/roadkeeper/ceilings.json, each held to its count until within 400; every other existing breach is a Suppression in eslint-suppressions.json, whose count per file and rule cannot grow. The issues that pay them off carry the deadline on their milestones (#149). The browser harness is the deep module scripts/browser/, and its entry, browser.mjs, is the one way in. Every browser case, deploy job and real-use check opens the site through walkSite, the browser walk: the built site served for it, or a live site's root address, at DESK or PHONE, in a fresh profile. It returns the walker's result, the layout shifts of the page it ends on (#269's first-input rule, read in layout-shifts/) and the pages' errors, each with its address, the first 100 kept. It fails when a page it draws is not the screen's width, and on the pages' errors unless the caller expects them. Beside it the entry offers chromePath and serve, kept for the server's own HTTP tests (#245): serve serves only what is inside its folder, so an escaped ../ or a link leading out is not found and a path it cannot decode is a bad request, and it can send a page's HTML in two pieces to test a paint mid-parse (#230). Inside, the page a walk hands over waits on what it reads, never a time: the page drawn, the page at rest (no animation, no smooth scroll going, no request in flight), a new document drawn, or a condition, with one 15 s backstop (tab/); the lint refuses a sleep in a test. A click or an Enter returns once the page has reported its first input, or another document stands: Chrome reports that input only once its frame is presented, after the shifts the measure reads (#269). BROWSER_CPU_SLOWDOWN slows every tab, and what a walk opens is closed however the process leaves (exit-register/). Each command under scripts/ is three files, one level each: the job (smoke.mjs, infrastructure) does the work and returns what it found, its CLI (cli-smoke.mjs, presentation) reads the arguments and words the result, and its entry (main-smoke.mjs, main) wires the two and is what package.json runs. The dev server knows the server it started is this project's by /countries.json, and reaches no screen word (#247). The carry (scripts/carry-assets) copies the live generation's assets into dist/, only from the site's own address and only bytes the previous build's digest list attests; it is a deep module whose entry, the flow, is given the live site, the build directory and the clock as ports. Its domain parts are private (generation/, outcome/, the ceilings in live-deploy/); its adapters and its log wording sit beside the command that wires them, and it never fails the deploy (#110, #199). Beside the build, the audit job reads the site's lockfile: an advisory reddens the run, never holds the deploy; only report waits on it, and runs whatever its result. report runs last, on a scheduled or dispatched run's first attempt, after the build, the deploy, the pin and the audit: a red keeps one issue, deploy run failed, and the first green closes it, through the data package's kept-issue CLI built from the commit data.lock names (#117). Both workflows run on a named image, ubuntu-26.04, never -latest (#24).
  • Pages — GitHub Pages at the custom domain, HTTPS enforced; static files only; the accepted cost is no response headers of our own.

Diagram 3 — the reader

  • Route page — rules in interview order, the rail with its label list, quotes with language and read date, the scope block, the data door (JSON, repository, tracker), one call to action that pre-scopes the interview. It dates only what it prints: each headline figure carries its own read date, and the stamp, the country cards and the liveness line read one set, the quotes the page prints. A site-wide page (/data/, /feedback/, the 404, the sitemap) dates the whole dataset, as the interview does (#76).
  • Interview — questions by information gain, then the verdict; runs entirely in the browser. The page is wiring alone: it builds the browser's history adapter and the record's store and starts the interview, one deep module, src/lib/interview/. Every decision a gesture leads to (the screen, its lines, how it meets the reader, the beat, the save, the history move) comes from one pure step, interviewAfter; the drawing only applies it. The drawing is a deep module nested in the interview, draw/, entered through drawing.ts's openDrawing (uncover, drawStep); the screens it draws and their parts (page, masthead, ledger, landing, beat, paint) are private under draw/screen/ (#261). The browser's history is a deep module of its own behind a port, interview-history, so Back across two tabs is tested in Node; Back names where it goes and never the screen it is on. The passport search is a module whose controller holds no DOM, country-search, and an arrival is one call, arrivalOf (#208). The verdict is one deep module, src/lib/verdict/ (#167): verdictOf decides everything the results screen says (the headline and masthead, the groups and their order, each card with its rail and gap, the steps, the job offer line, the arranged line, the folds) and verdictHtml draws it, with its own stylesheet; the interview only paints, announces and records one history entry per verdict. Steps are only what the reader can do; what a job offer would open and what someone else arranges are said beside them, never counted as steps. Inside the verdict, its reckoning is application and makes no word, the dataset's included: in-view.ts and steps.ts say which results are in view, which steps there are and what each arranged answer or a job offer would open, and the presentation files around them name it (#183). A Card is one deep module inside it, compose/card (#184): its entry, cards.ts, draws a route's card, a Not yet row, a closed row, a step's card and a Notice's card, and its blocks (the route statements, the rail, the provenance) are private behind it. A money shortfall is decided at application, in numbers, by money-shortfall.ts; printed-shortfall.ts formats its amounts once, and copy/verdict.ts says it side by side as the card's note, a step's reach and the headline's emphasis. Every word a screen prints lives in src/lib/copy/, one file per screen or part, read by name. Its first paint is one module, src/lib/first-paint.ts (#66). An inline head script reads the record, the link and the width before anything paints, and writes a cover and the first-paint seeds on <html>. The stylesheet it renders hides what each cover hides. The interview takes the covers off once, as it draws the reader's first screen, so no arrival moves the page. The box takes no room until the ledger after it is parsed, so a page arriving in pieces paints where it stays (#236). The masthead has one writer per screen: a question screen's is questionMastheadOf, beside the question card; a results or notice screen's is composed inside the verdict module and carried by the screen as data, so no question screen can carry a claim about a comparison (#172). Its own markup is one emphasis, and every other word, the dataset's included, is escaped (#25). A question card a gesture draws comes with a beat: it fades in, and for --motion-beat (tokens.css) every commit of an answer, click or Enter, is refused in one place, motion or none. The first paint and the verdict have none (#86). A question fewer than all the open routes read carries its asked-for line, drawn from reckonAskingRoutes: the routes by name and country, or counted per country past two. A pencil change of answer replays the interview, and the answers no route reads any more are named once as set aside in the declared panel (its folded summary on a phone); a money row answered "Doesn't apply…" keeps its pencil (#133). Every screen but /data/ speaks the reader's words, not the model's: no "scored", "rule set" or "this interview" (GLOSSARY, Scope statement). A link to a source says whose page it is ("Official page", or "Consolidated text on buzer.de"); an abbreviation is explained the first time each page uses it (src/lib/gloss.ts, results cards included); a criterion with paths is headed by its label with one line per path; the passport search answers a territory with the passport its people hold. One walk over every page the build draws (tests/reader-pages.ts) holds these (#151).
  • Record — localStorage (legacy key migrated) or nothing; a print stylesheet for a paper copy. A record longer than any the page writes (8 KB) is no record, and is never parsed (#25). Start over clears it on every address: a shared device keeps nothing of a reader (#208).
  • Tracker — permit-rulebook-data/issues with bug, design-flaw, new-need; reached only by the reader's own click.

Not yet real-green (s6): the phone walk on the live site, the isolated v1-gate critique's blockers cleared, and the announcement.
